ports.name: Porto Novo
ports.description: A bustling harbor city, gateway to inland trade. Grain ships fill the docks.

ports.name: Al-Manar
ports.description: Ancient port famed for its spice markets. Merchants bid fiercely for grain and iron.

ports.name: Silva Bay
ports.description: Timber-rich bay surrounded by dense forests. The shipwrights here are the best in the region.

ports.name: Corsair's Rest
ports.description: A lawless harbor tucked between cliffs. Smugglers, pirates, and those who trade with them.

ports.name: Ironhaven
ports.description: Industrial port city wreathed in forge smoke. Weapons and iron flow out, everything else flows in.

ports.name: Stormwall
ports.description: Fortress port guarding the northern straits. Military outpost with strict inspections.

ports.name: Thornport
ports.description: Whaling town turned trading post. Tea and tobacco are the local currency. Medicines fetch gold.

ports.name: Sun Harbor
ports.description: Golden coast port where cotton bales stack higher than the warehouses.

ports.name: Palm Cove
ports.description: A sheltered cove where rum barrels outnumber the inhabitants. Cheapest provisions on the coast.

ports.name: Iron Point
ports.description: Mining settlement at the river mouth. Iron flows out, everything else flows in at a premium.

ports.name: Pearl Shallows
ports.description: Divers bring up pearls from the warm shallows. A quiet port where fortunes are made by the patient.

ports.name: Jade Port
ports.description: Porcelain workshops line the waterfront. Iron and grain are worth their weight in gold here.

ports.name: Monsoon Reach
ports.description: Seasonal winds funnel the spice trade through this crossroads. The shipyard builds for endurance.

ports.name: Silk Haven
ports.description: Premier silk market of the eastern waters. Rum and iron are scarce luxuries here.

ports.name: Crosswind Isle
ports.description: Free port at the junction of all trade winds. Everything passes through, nothing stays cheap.

ports.name: Dragon's Gate
ports.description: Fortress harbor controlling the eastern straits. Weapons are contraband here, but medicines are gold.

ports.name: Spice Narrows
ports.description: Hidden anchorage in the spice archipelago. The most concentrated spice market in the world.

ports.name: Ember Isle
ports.description: Volcanic island with obsidian beaches. Rich in rare minerals and medicinal plants.

ports.name: Typhoon Anchorage
ports.description: Storm-battered harbor that only the boldest captains visit. Pearls and rare goods reward the brave.

ports.name: Coral Throne
ports.description: Island kingdom built on coral reefs. The king trades pearls for weapons and demands tribute in silk.

routes.lore: The oldest trade route in the Mediterranean. Grain ships have sailed this lane since before memory.
Short and safe — the shipwrights' lifeline. Silva Bay's timber built Porto Novo's fleet.
Every merchant denies using it. Every merchant uses it. The line between trade and smuggling runs through these waters.
Iron from the foundries, soldiers from the fortress. This lane never sleeps.
Thornport's warmth heading to Stormwall's cold. The northern comfort trade.
Mediterranean grain south, Gold Coast cotton north. The route that clothed an empire.
Months of open water. The route that separates traders from merchants. Many set out. Fewer arrive.
From the free port to the kiln masters. Every piece of porcelain in the west passed through here.
Where porcelain meets silk. The two oldest trades in the East, connected by the shortest route.
Named for obvious reasons. The monsoon winds funnel through here like a gauntlet. Timing is survival.
Warm currents and sulfur air. The locals say the sea boils near the islands on bad days.
Timing is everything. Catch the monsoon right and you fly. Catch it wrong and you drown.
Only the desperate or the bold sail this direct. Pirate kings once controlled both ends.
Iron west, porcelain east. The longest profitable route in the world.
Pearl to pearl. The divers of the shallows and the divers of the reef — same craft, different kingdoms.

contracts.description: A port needs grain shipments to feed its population.
contracts.cultural_flavor: The granaries are nearly empty. Without this shipment, the city faces a hungry winter.

contracts.description: A shipyard needs timber to fill construction orders.
Forges and workshops need iron ore delivered.
A port urgently needs medical supplies.
contracts.cultural_flavor: The fever wards are full. Healers work without rest. Every crate of medicine is a life saved.

contracts.description: A military outpost needs arms delivered. Discretion optional.
contracts.cultural_flavor: The fortress needs arms. Don't ask what they're for. The garrison pays well and asks no questions.

contracts.description: Stocks are critically low. Urgent grain delivery needed.
The port's rum stocks are dangerously low. Sailors are restless.
Tea supplies have dried up. The population demands resupply.

contracts.title_pattern: Silk for a private buyer at {destination}
contracts.description: A wealthy collector wants silk delivered quietly.
contracts.cultural_flavor: The governor's daughter is to be married. Only the finest silk will do. Speak of this to no one.

contracts.description: A noble estate requires fine porcelain. Discretion expected.
A spice monopolist needs off-the-books supply. High scrutiny.
contracts.cultural_flavor: The Spice Lords control every legal channel. This shipment goes around them. They will not be pleased.

contracts.title_pattern: Pearls for a royal court at {destination}
contracts.description: A crowned head seeks the finest pearls. The reward is as magnificent as the risk.
contracts.cultural_flavor: These pearls will adorn a crown. The divers who found them will never know. That is the way of kings.

contracts.description: Cotton surplus needs to move. Pays for the backhaul.
A merchant house needs spice moved from origin stockpile.
Textile manufacturers need dyes from the African coast.
Complete a Mediterranean-West Africa trade loop. Deliver goods to prove the route.
Prove the East Indies trade route with a delivery run.
Blaze a trade route to the South Seas. Few have returned with profit.
contracts.cultural_flavor: The South Seas are uncharted profit. Bring back their treasures and your name will be legend.

contracts.description: A premium charter for an established captain. Trust and standing required.
contracts.cultural_flavor: The Exchange Guild only charters captains they trust absolutely. This contract is a mark of honor.

contracts.description: A prestigious North Atlantic trade charter. Only for captains of proven reputation.
The Syndicate needs opium moved from Spice Narrows. Inspection means prison. Success means fortune.
contracts.cultural_flavor: The Monsoon Syndicate controls every pipe of opium east of Crosswind Isle. This shipment goes west. Don't get caught.

contracts.description: Military-grade powder, no questions asked. Deliver to the specified port before the garrison gets suspicious.
contracts.cultural_flavor: Someone needs powder and they need it quiet. The fewer questions you ask, the higher you get paid.

contracts.description: Liberated cargo needs a buyer. Move it to a black market port and make it disappear.
contracts.cultural_flavor: The Brotherhood took a merchant's cargo last week. Now it needs to vanish. That's where you come in.

contracts.description: A pirate faction needs weapons and rum delivered to their territory. Official channels won't touch this.
contracts.cultural_flavor: The faction that controls these waters needs resupply. Help them, and you'll have friends where others have enemies.

armor.name: Leather Vest
armor.description: Stiff cowhide shaped to the torso. Won't stop a bullet, but a blade has to work for it.

armor.name: Padded Coat
armor.description: Layered cotton quilting over a wool core. Surprisingly effective against slashing attacks.

armor.name: Chain Shirt
armor.description: Riveted iron rings over a linen undershirt. The weight is real, but so is the protection.

armor.name: Brigandine
armor.description: Small steel plates riveted between layers of cloth. Eastern craftsmanship, flexible and quiet.

armor.name: Coconut Fiber Armor
armor.description: Woven coconut husk and pandanus leaves, layered thick. Surprisingly tough against blades, and it floats.

armor.name: Steel Cuirass
armor.description: A hammered breastplate from a Northern foundry. You feel every ounce, but blades bounce off.

melee_weapons.name: Cutlass
melee_weapons.description: The sailor's sword. Short, curved, and built for close quarters on a rolling deck.

melee_weapons.name: Rapier
melee_weapons.description: A long, thin thrusting sword. Devastating in trained hands, awkward in untrained ones.

melee_weapons.name: Boarding Axe
melee_weapons.description: Half hatchet, half hook. Made for cutting ropes and skulls in equal measure.

melee_weapons.name: Dagger
melee_weapons.description: A short blade for close work. Fast in the hand, light on the belt.

melee_weapons.name: Kris
melee_weapons.description: A wavy-bladed dagger of spiritual significance. Every kris has a name and a history.

melee_weapons.name: Ida Sword
melee_weapons.description: A broad, leaf-shaped blade from the Yoruba kingdoms. Built for powerful slashing arcs.

melee_weapons.name: Leiomano
melee_weapons.description: A war club edged with shark teeth. The wounds it leaves never heal cleanly.

melee_weapons.name: Halberd
melee_weapons.description: An axe blade on a six-foot shaft. Reach and power, but slow in tight spaces.

ranged_weapons.name: Matchlock Pistol
ranged_weapons.description: A clumsy but devastating single-shot pistol. The slow match glows in the dark.

ranged_weapons.name: Wheellock Pistol
ranged_weapons.description: German engineering. The spring-wound mechanism fires faster and more reliably than matchlock.

ranged_weapons.name: Arquebus Pistol
ranged_weapons.description: A Portuguese trade pistol, common wherever the carracks sailed. Rough but reliable.

ranged_weapons.name: Hand Crossbow
ranged_weapons.description: A compact crossbow that fits in a belt holster. Silent and accurate, but slow to reload.

ranged_weapons.name: Throwing Knife
ranged_weapons.description: A balanced blade weighted for throwing. Cheap, silent, disposable.

ranged_weapons.name: Sling
ranged_weapons.description: A leather sling and smooth stones. Ancient, effective, and completely silent.

ranged_weapons.name: Blowgun
ranged_weapons.description: A slender bamboo tube firing poisoned darts. Almost no damage, but the toxin weakens. Silent as breath.

ranged_weapons.name: Bolas
ranged_weapons.description: Three weighted stones on cord. Wraps around legs, arms, or weapons. More disabling than damaging.

fighting_styles.name: La Destreza
fighting_styles.description: The Spanish science of defense. Every movement calculated, every thrust placed with geometric precision.
fighting_styles.historical_note: Systematized by Jeronimo Sanchez de Carranza in 1569. The first European martial art treated as an academic discipline.

special_action.name: Estocada
special_action.flavor: A geometric thrust — the blade finds the only open line.

fighting_styles.name: Highland Broadsword
fighting_styles.description: The broadsword tradition of the Scottish Highlands and Norse raiders. No finesse, no subtlety — overwhelming force.
fighting_styles.historical_note: Highland sword-and-targe techniques documented across Scotland and Scandinavia. The two-handed claymore was already legendary by the 1500s.

special_action.name: Cleave
special_action.flavor: A devastating overhead arc that shatters guards and bones alike.

fighting_styles.name: Dambe
fighting_styles.description: The fighting art of the Hausa people. The lead fist is the spear, the rear hand is the shield, and the legs finish every fight.
fighting_styles.historical_note: Practiced across West Africa since at least the 15th century. Dambe bouts were a central part of harvest festivals and market days.

special_action.name: Leg Sweep
special_action.flavor: A low spinning sweep — the opponent's legs are taken from under them. They crash to the deck.

fighting_styles.name: Silat
fighting_styles.description: The blade and grappling art of the Malay Archipelago. Low stances, curved blades, trapping hands, and devastating close-range techniques.
fighting_styles.historical_note: Pencak Silat was already ancient when Portuguese traders first documented it in the 1500s. The kris dagger is both weapon and cultural artifact.

special_action.name: Keris Strike
special_action.flavor: The curved kris finds the gap between guard and grip — the opponent's weapon arm goes numb.

fighting_styles.name: Lua
fighting_styles.description: The bone-breaking art of Polynesia. Joint locks, pressure points, and techniques designed not to wound but to permanently disable.
fighting_styles.historical_note: Hawaiian Lua was restricted to the warrior class. Its techniques were so dangerous that training was conducted in secret, at night, under oath.

special_action.name: Joint Lock
special_action.flavor: You seize the opponent's arm and twist. Bone grinds against joint. They can only writhe and dodge.

skills.name: Blacksmithing
skills.description: The art of metalwork — maintaining, repairing, and improving weapons and armor.

levels.name: Apprentice
levels.description: Basic maintenance. Reduce maintenance costs by 25%. Degradation slowed by 20%.

levels.name: Journeyman
levels.description: Field repairs at sea. Reduce maintenance costs by 50%. Degradation slowed by 40%. Can restore worn weapons to standard at sea.

levels.name: Master
levels.description: Master craftsman. Maintenance costs halved. Degradation slowed by 60%. Smith upgrades cost 25% less. Field repairs restore to standard.

trainers.name: Forge Master Erik
trainers.description: The best smith in the North Atlantic. His blades hold an edge for years.
trainers.dialog: "Steel remembers every hammer blow. I'll teach your hands to speak its language."

trainers.name: Old Vasquez
trainers.description: A retired armorer who sharpens blades in the harbor market. Fast and cheap, but not a master.
trainers.dialog: "I can teach you to keep a blade sharp and a pistol clean. That's worth more than fancy swordplay."

trainers.name: The Silva Bay Smithy
trainers.description: A family of shipwrights who also forge the finest blades in the Mediterranean.
trainers.dialog: "We build ships and swords from the same iron. Both need to survive the sea."

trainers.name: Rajan the Tinker
trainers.description: An East Indies metalworker who repairs anything from kris daggers to Portuguese cannons.
trainers.dialog: "Every weapon that passes through this port, I have fixed. Bring me yours."

trainers.name: Kai the Shaper
trainers.description: A young smith who learned from sailors. Basic work, but honest.
trainers.dialog: "I'm no master, but I can keep your steel from rusting in the salt air. That's something."

roles.name: Marine
roles.description: A trained fighter who stands at your side in combat.

roles.name: Navigator
roles.description: Reads the stars and currents. Gets you there faster and safer.

roles.name: Surgeon
roles.description: Keeps crew alive and your wounds clean.

roles.name: Smuggler
roles.description: Knows every hidden compartment and customs loophole.

roles.name: Quartermaster
roles.description: Manages cargo, negotiates prices, and counts every coin.

companions.name: Iron Marta
companions.description: A former garrison soldier who deserted for the sea. Fights like she has nothing to lose.
companions.greeting: A woman in a soldier's coat sits alone at the bar, sharpening a boarding axe.
companions.hire_dialog: "I've been looking for a captain worth fighting for. Pay's secondary. Show me you're not a coward."
companions.loyalty_line: "Best decision I ever made, signing on with you."
companions.warning_line: "Captain... I'm starting to wonder if this ship is heading anywhere worth going."
companions.departure_line: "I didn't leave the garrison to follow another fool. I'm done."

companions.name: Red Tomas
companions.description: A pirate-turned-bodyguard with a face full of scars and a code of honor.
companions.greeting: A scarred man watches you from the corner. His hand never leaves the cutlass at his belt.
companions.hire_dialog: "I protect. You pay. Simple arrangement. Betray me and you'll wish the pirates found you first."
companions.loyalty_line: "You're straight with me, Captain. That's rare on these waters."
companions.warning_line: "This isn't what I signed up for. We need to talk."
companions.departure_line: "The deal's off. Don't look for me."

companions.name: Star Lila
companions.description: A Javanese navigator who reads the stars like others read books. She's never been lost.
companions.greeting: A young woman sits on the dock, sketching star charts on palm bark with quiet concentration.
companions.hire_dialog: "The stars brought me here. Perhaps they brought you too. I'll navigate — you decide where."
companions.loyalty_line: "The stars say we're on the right path. I believe them."
companions.warning_line: "The currents are wrong, Captain. Not the sea — this ship's course."
companions.departure_line: "The stars say it's time to part. I wish you fair winds."

companions.name: Old Henry
companions.description: Fifty years at sea. He's sailed every route twice and remembers every reef.
companions.greeting: An old man mends nets by the harbor, humming a tune you don't recognize. His eyes are sharp.
companions.hire_dialog: "I'm too old to captain my own ship, but I'm not too old to keep yours off the rocks. Deal?"
companions.loyalty_line: "Reminds me of the old days. Good captain, good ship, good sea."
companions.warning_line: "I've seen captains make these mistakes before. It doesn't end well."
companions.departure_line: "I'm retiring. For real this time. Good luck, Captain."

companions.name: Dr. Amara
companions.description: A healer trained in both Western and African medicine. She's saved more lives than most doctors dream of.
companions.greeting: A woman in a clean apron tends to a sailor's wound at the dockside clinic. Efficient, gentle hands.
companions.hire_dialog: "I go where people need healing. Your crew looks like they could use it. I have conditions — no unnecessary cruelty."
companions.loyalty_line: "Your crew trusts you. That's the best medicine there is."
companions.warning_line: "I became a healer to save lives, Captain. Not to watch them wasted."
companions.departure_line: "I cannot stay on a ship that causes more harm than it heals. Goodbye, Captain."

companions.name: Patches
companions.description: A ship's surgeon who earned his nickname from the number of wounds he's stitched. Drinks too much, but his hands are steady.
companions.greeting: A man with rum-stained fingers and a surgeon's kit sits at the bar. He's stitching his own thumb.
companions.hire_dialog: "I can keep your crew alive. Mostly. I charge cheap because I drink the medicine budget. Fair warning."
companions.loyalty_line: "Best gig I've had in years. The rum's flowing and nobody's dying."
companions.warning_line: "I'm a doctor, not a miracle worker. This ship needs better luck — or a better captain."
companions.departure_line: "I'm finding a quieter ship. One where I can drink in peace."

companions.name: Shadow Kai
companions.description: Nobody knows his real name. He makes contraband disappear and reappear wherever it needs to be.
companions.greeting: A man you didn't notice before is suddenly standing beside you. "Looking for someone discreet?"
companions.hire_dialog: "I have skills. You have cargo holds. Let's make each other rich. Just don't ask where things go."
companions.loyalty_line: "Good captain. Doesn't ask stupid questions. My kind of arrangement."
companions.warning_line: "You're drawing too much heat. That's bad for business — and for my neck."
companions.departure_line: "The arrangement is over. You'll never see me again. That's the point."

companions.name: Rosa the Fence
companions.description: A woman who knows the price of everything and the customs schedule of every port.
companions.greeting: A woman with too many rings counts coins at a corner table. She's been watching you since you walked in.
companions.hire_dialog: "Every captain needs someone who knows where the inspectors aren't. That's me. Fifty-fifty on the extras."
companions.loyalty_line: "We're making good silver together. Long may it last."
companions.warning_line: "The margins are getting thin and the heat's getting thick. Watch yourself."
companions.departure_line: "Bad for business, Captain. I'm moving on before your luck runs out on both of us."

companions.name: Coin Mariam
companions.description: A merchant's daughter who can appraise cargo by smell and negotiate prices in seven languages.
companions.greeting: A well-dressed woman inspects cargo manifests at the harbormaster's office. She spots errors in seconds.
companions.hire_dialog: "Your books are a mess. Your cargo holds are inefficient. Your pricing is amateur. Hire me and I'll fix all three."
companions.loyalty_line: "The ledgers are clean, the holds are full, and the silver is flowing. My kind of ship."
companions.warning_line: "The numbers don't lie, Captain. We're heading for a loss if you keep this up."
companions.departure_line: "I don't serve captains who ignore the ledger. Find another quartermaster."

companions.name: Dockhand Pete
companions.description: Knows every dock, every scale, and every harbormaster's weakness on the West African coast.
companions.greeting: A wiry man balances on a cargo crate, juggling oranges. He catches all three without looking.
companions.hire_dialog: "I know cargo. I know ports. I know who's cheating on the scales. Hire me and you'll never overpay for grain again."
companions.loyalty_line: "Good ship, good captain, good cargo. Life's good!"
companions.warning_line: "Captain, I'm starting to feel like ballast. Use me or lose me."
companions.departure_line: "I need a ship that's actually going somewhere. No hard feelings."

merchants.name: Marco
merchants.title: Master Weaponsmith
merchants.description: A stocky Genoese smith with oil-stained hands and a shop full of blades hanging from the ceiling.
merchants.greeting: Ah, a captain with taste! Come, see what Marco has forged this week.

merchants.name: Fatima
merchants.title: Armorer
merchants.description: She runs the finest armor workshop south of the strait. Her chain is tight and her prices tighter.
merchants.greeting: You want protection? Protection costs. But so does a funeral.

merchants.name: Old Silva
merchants.title: Ship Outfitter
merchants.description: A retired shipwright who sells what sailors need. His shop smells of tar and salt.
merchants.greeting: What do you need. I have it or I don't.

merchants.name: Sgt. Gruber
merchants.title: Arsenal Master
merchants.description: A retired dragoon who sells military-grade equipment from a fortress-turned-shop.
merchants.greeting: State your business. I don't sell to tourists.

merchants.name: Widow Kael
merchants.title: Outfitter
merchants.description: She inherited her husband's shop when he didn't come back from the ice. She knows every item by touch.
merchants.greeting: The wind's picking up. Buy what you need before it gets worse.

merchants.name: Hamish
merchants.title: Bladesmith
merchants.description: A Highland smith who forges axes and broadswords in a workshop built into the cliff face.
merchants.greeting: If it's sharp and it swings, I made it. If it's dull, someone else made it.

merchants.name: Adaeze
merchants.title: Arms Dealer
merchants.description: A trader's daughter who turned her father's cloth stall into a weapons bazaar. She haggles like she breathes.
merchants.greeting: Welcome, captain! Everything you see is the best in the harbor. I should know — I tested it myself.

merchants.name: Kofi
merchants.title: Leatherworker
merchants.description: He works crocodile hide into armor that turns blades. His fingers are scarred from the stitching awl.
merchants.greeting: Good leather takes time. I have what's ready.

merchants.name: Yaa
merchants.title: Blade Merchant
merchants.description: She sources knives and slings from inland villages and sells them to sailors at the dock.
merchants.greeting: Pearl Shallows has the best steel on the coast. Don't let anyone tell you otherwise.

merchants.name: Master Chen
merchants.title: Master Smith
merchants.description: Third generation bladesmith. His kris daggers are considered sacred objects in three kingdoms.
merchants.greeting: A captain who values craftsmanship. Please, examine my work.

merchants.name: Devi
merchants.title: Armorer
merchants.description: She imports brigandine plates from the mainland and fits them in her harbor-side workshop.
merchants.greeting: Monsoon season is coming. You'll want something between you and the sea.

merchants.name: Li Wei
merchants.title: Mechanist
merchants.description: A craftsman who builds hand crossbows from bamboo and horn. Quiet weapons for quiet work.
merchants.greeting: Silk Haven values discretion. So do my weapons.

merchants.name: Tane
merchants.title: Warrior Outfitter
merchants.description: A former reef warrior who now outfits captains with the weapons of his people.
merchants.greeting: The reef teaches you to fight or it teaches you to drown. Which are you?

merchants.name: Malia
merchants.title: Outfitter
merchants.description: She runs the only proper shop between the reefs. If she doesn't have it, you don't need it.
merchants.greeting: Typhoon Anchorage! Where the brave come to buy and the foolish come to sell.

style_masters.name: Maestro Luciano
style_masters.description: A retired fencing master who teaches the Spanish school from a warehouse overlooking the harbor.
style_masters.dialog: "The sword is a compass. Your body is the circle. Step correctly and no blade can touch you."

style_masters.name: Señora Vega
style_masters.description: A Castilian expatriate who runs the only fencing school east of Gibraltar.
style_masters.dialog: "You fight like a dockhand. I will teach you to fight like a mathematician."

style_masters.name: Red Hamish
style_masters.description: A massive Scotsman with arms like anchor chains. He teaches broadsword in the foundry yard, sparking steel against iron.
style_masters.dialog: "Ye dinnae need fancy footwork when ye can split a man's shield in two. Hit harder. Again."

style_masters.name: Jarl Solveig
style_masters.description: A Norse shieldmaiden who settled in Thornport after twenty years of raiding. She teaches the old ways.
style_masters.dialog: "The broadsword is not a weapon. It is a statement. When you swing, mean it."

style_masters.name: Kolo the Fist
style_masters.description: A retired champion whose wrapped fists have broken more guards than any siege engine. He teaches on the beach at dawn.
style_masters.dialog: "The spear fist strikes. The shield hand protects. The leg decides. Simple. Now do it a thousand times."

style_masters.name: Nneka Ironfist
style_masters.description: A woman who earned her name in the fighting circles of the Gold Coast. She teaches with bruises, not words.
style_masters.dialog: "You think fighting is about your arms? Your legs carry the fight. Everything begins from the ground."

style_masters.name: Pak Reza
style_masters.description: An elderly silat master who moves like smoke. His school is hidden behind a porcelain shop.
style_masters.dialog: "The kris is not a sword. It does not cut — it finds. Every body has openings. I will teach you to see them."

style_masters.name: Dewi Ayu
style_masters.description: A trader's daughter who learned silat from her grandmother. She teaches in the monsoon rain because 'the deck is always wet.'
style_masters.dialog: "Western fencing stands tall and proud. Silat crouches low and survives. Which do you think lasts longer at sea?"

style_masters.name: Kahoku the Elder
style_masters.description: An ancient warrior-priest whose hands have set more bones than any doctor — because he broke them first.
style_masters.dialog: "Lua was never meant for sport. Every hold is designed to end a fight permanently. Are you certain you want this knowledge?"

style_masters.name: Leilani Bonecatcher
style_masters.description: A young woman with an old name. She learned Lua from her grandfather and teaches it to those the sea has tested.
style_masters.dialog: "The bones tell you everything. How strong they are, where they bend, where they break. Listen to the bones."

milestones.name: First Warehouse
milestones.description: Leased your first warehouse — cargo can now be staged for timing plays.

milestones.name: First Broker Office
milestones.description: Opened your first broker office — intelligence shapes the contract board.

milestones.name: Regional Standing
milestones.description: Reached meaningful standing in one region through consistent commerce.

milestones.name: Strong Regional Presence
milestones.description: Achieved strong standing in one region — a known and respected operator.

milestones.name: Two-Region Presence
milestones.description: Established operations in two different regions.

milestones.name: Credible Operator
milestones.description: The market recognizes you as credible — new opportunities open.

milestones.name: Reliable Operator
milestones.description: Reliable commercial trust — premium contracts and better credit terms.

milestones.name: First Regional Charter
milestones.description: Acquired your first regional trade charter — formal commercial standing.

milestones.name: High Reputation Charter
milestones.description: Earned the highest commercial charter — recognized across all regions.

milestones.name: Proven Contract Record
milestones.description: Completed 5+ contracts — a track record of reliable delivery.

milestones.name: Clean Growth
milestones.description: Reached reliable trust while keeping heat low — growth without suspicion.

milestones.name: First Discreet Delivery
milestones.description: Completed your first discreet luxury delivery — the shadow lane is open.

milestones.name: Operating Under Scrutiny
milestones.description: Sustained high heat while remaining profitable — the authorities watch, but you persist.

milestones.name: Shadow Profitability
milestones.description: Strong net profit despite elevated customs scrutiny.

milestones.name: Seizure Recovery
milestones.description: Survived a cargo seizure and rebuilt — the business endures.

milestones.name: East Indies Access
milestones.description: Acquired the East Indies Access Charter — the far trade routes are open.

milestones.name: East Indies Presence
milestones.description: Opened a broker office in the East Indies — local intelligence secured.

milestones.name: Galleon Operator
milestones.description: Operating a Merchant Galleon — the long-haul workhorse.

milestones.name: East Indies Reputation
milestones.description: Strong standing in the East Indies — a known operator in the spice quarter.

milestones.name: First Insurance Payout
milestones.description: An insurance claim was paid — risk pricing proves its worth.

milestones.name: First Credit Draw
milestones.description: Drew on a credit line — leverage is now part of the business.

milestones.name: Clean Credit Record
milestones.description: Significant borrowing with no defaults — the market trusts your debt service.

milestones.name: Leveraged Expansion
milestones.description: Used credit to fund infrastructure growth — capital working for capital.

milestones.name: Multi-Region Infrastructure
milestones.description: Infrastructure assets across multiple regions — a commercial network.

milestones.name: Cross-Region Contract House
milestones.description: 5+ contracts completed with standing in 2+ regions.

milestones.name: Full-Spectrum Operation
milestones.description: Using warehouses, brokers, licenses, insurance, and credit — a complete commercial toolkit.

milestones.name: Ship Upgrade
milestones.description: Upgraded beyond the starting sloop — the business justified the investment.

warehouse_tiers.name: Small Depot
warehouse_tiers.description: A rented corner of a dockside warehouse. Enough to stage a few crates.

warehouse_tiers.name: Regional Warehouse
warehouse_tiers.description: A proper warehouse with your name on the door. Real staging capacity.

warehouse_tiers.name: Commercial Warehouse
warehouse_tiers.description: A merchant house warehouse. Full commercial staging operation.

brokers.name: Mediterranean Local Broker
brokers.description: A clerk in the harbor exchange. Knows who's buying what.

brokers.name: Mediterranean Broker House
brokers.description: A proper merchant's office overlooking the quay. Charter work flows through here.

brokers.name: North Atlantic Local Broker
brokers.description: An Iron Pact clerk at the garrison exchange. Weapons boards and winter stores.

brokers.name: North Atlantic Garrison House
brokers.description: An Iron Pact house beside the arsenal. Garrison contracts and storm-season provisioning.

brokers.name: West Africa Local Broker
brokers.description: A trader's agent at the coast. Knows the staple routes cold.

brokers.name: West Africa Trade Office
brokers.description: A permanent office with warehousing contacts. Return freight is the specialty.

brokers.name: East Indies Local Broker
brokers.description: A factor's contact in the spice quarter. Luxury connections.

brokers.name: East Indies Trading House
brokers.description: A merchant house with direct connections to silk and spice guilds. The serious money flows here.

brokers.name: South Seas Local Broker
brokers.description: A Coral Crown factor on the reef quay. Tribute first; pearls and weapons follow.

brokers.name: South Seas Tribute House
brokers.description: A Coral Crown house that prices tribute, premium pearls, and steel. Typhoon windows are the specialty.

licenses.name: Mediterranean Trade Charter
licenses.description: Formal authorization for commercial shipping in Mediterranean waters. Opens lawful procurement contracts and reduces customs friction.

licenses.name: North Atlantic Iron Charter
licenses.description: Iron Pact authorization for garrison and weapons shipping in North Atlantic waters. Opens lawful procurement boards and eases Stormwall inspections.

licenses.name: West Africa Commerce Permit
licenses.description: Trading permit recognized along the West African coast. Unlocks staple procurement contracts and return freight priority.

licenses.name: East Indies Access Charter
licenses.description: Permission to trade freely in East Indies ports. Opens long-haul circuit contracts and premium cargo access.

licenses.name: South Seas Reef Charter
licenses.description: Coral Crown permission to offer tribute and trade in South Seas waters. Opens premium pearl and weapons boards on the reef circuits.

licenses.name: Luxury Goods Permit
licenses.description: Cross-regional authorization for luxury commodity trading. Grants access to discreet luxury contracts everywhere.

licenses.name: High Reputation Commercial Charter
licenses.description: Elite commercial authorization recognized in all regions. Highest-tier contract board quality and customs privilege.

policies.name: Basic Hull Insurance
policies.description: Covers storm and pirate damage to ship hull. Partial coverage — reduces repair costs, not eliminates them.

policies.name: Comprehensive Hull Insurance
policies.description: Full hull protection for serious operators. Higher coverage and cap, but requires clean reputation.

policies.name: Standard Cargo Insurance
policies.description: Covers cargo loss from storms, piracy, and inspection seizure. Contraband is excluded.

policies.name: Premium Cargo Insurance
policies.description: High-coverage protection for luxury cargo runs. Requires low heat. Contraband excluded.

policies.name: Contract Guarantee — Basic
policies.description: Covers part of the penalty if a contract fails or expires. Tied to a specific contract.

policies.name: Contract Guarantee — Full
policies.description: Strong contract protection for high-value obligations. Requires clean reputation and established trust.

credit_tiers.name: Merchant Line
credit_tiers.description: Entry-level working capital. Enough to bridge one cargo purchase or provision a long voyage. Modest limit, moderate interest.

credit_tiers.name: House Credit
credit_tiers.description: Serious working capital backed by commercial reputation. Fund larger cargo positions or infrastructure investments.

credit_tiers.name: Premier Commercial Line
credit_tiers.description: Top-tier leverage for established operators. Fund entire trade campaigns. Best rate, but default destroys reputation.

port_institutions.power_structure: Porto Novo is governed by Senhora Costa, but real power is triangulated: Costa sets policy, Marta controls prices through the Exchange Guild, and Salva enforces the law. Dimitri's shipyard is independent — the Brotherhood answers to craft, not politics. Old Enzo's tavern is the shadow channel where information flows that the official institutions pretend doesn't exist. Fernanda's broker desk is where policy meets practice — she decides which contracts reach which captains.
port_institutions.internal_tension: The core tension is between Marta and Costa. Marta wants market dominance — she'd squeeze every margin to make the Exchange richer. Costa wants political stability — she'd sacrifice some profit for Alliance cohesion. They need each other: Costa can't govern without the Guild's revenue, and Marta can't trade without Costa's political protection. The tension keeps Porto Novo honest. Meanwhile, Old Enzo quietly facilitates the grey economy that neither woman acknowledges exists, and Inspector Salva watches everything with the patience of a man who knows that sooner or later, everyone makes a mistake.

institutions.name: The Harbor Master's Tower
institutions.description: A stone tower at the harbor mouth with a brass telescope on the roof and a ledger room that smells of ink and sealing wax. Every ship is logged, every berth assigned, every fee collected here.
institutions.function: Controls docking, assigns berths, collects port fees. Clean records earn faster processing.
institutions.political_leaning: Alliance loyalist. Vasco runs a tight harbor that reflects Alliance standards.

institutions.name: The Grain Exchange
institutions.description: A columned hall on the waterfront — the largest building in Porto Novo. Dawn rates are read from the steps every morning. Inside, the trading floor hums with negotiation, and the air smells of grain dust and ambition.
institutions.function: Sets daily prices, arbitrates trade disputes, manages market slots. The Alliance's economic heart.
institutions.political_leaning: The Exchange IS the Alliance. Marta's policies are Alliance policies.

institutions.name: Andros & Sons Shipyard
institutions.description: A sprawling yard of slipways, sawpits, and dry docks. The sound of adzes and hammers never stops. Three hulls are always under construction. The sign reads 'Andros & Sons' but the sons are long grown and it's just Dimitri now, with his apprentices.
institutions.function: Ship repairs, upgrades, and purchases. Quality work at fair prices — but Dimitri judges your seamanship.
institutions.political_leaning: Apolitical. Dimitri builds for anyone who respects ships. Except warmongers.

institutions.name: The Governor's Residence
institutions.description: A modest stone house overlooking the harbor, distinguished only by the Exchange Alliance banner hanging from the balcony. Costa governs from a desk covered in charts and correspondence. No throne, no court — just a woman who works.
institutions.function: Sets port policy, approves trade agreements, manages Alliance relations. The political center.
institutions.political_leaning: Alliance core. Costa's policies shape the entire Mediterranean legitimate trade.

institutions.name: The Harbor Bell
institutions.description: A low-ceilinged tavern built from ship timbers, with a salvaged bell hanging over the door. It's always too warm, too loud, and too crowded. The food is terrible. The rum is excellent. Everyone comes here.
institutions.function: Crew recruitment, rumors, underworld contacts. The social hub where deals begin before they're official.
institutions.political_leaning: Neutral — Enzo serves all sides, which makes him useful to everyone and trusted by no one.

institutions.name: The Customs House
institutions.description: A clean, whitewashed building near the docks with iron bars on every window and a locked evidence room in the basement. The waiting bench outside is the most feared seat in Porto Novo.
institutions.function: Cargo inspection, tariff collection, contraband seizure. Clean captains pass quickly. Others don't.
institutions.political_leaning: Alliance enforcer. Salva enforces Alliance trade law with personal intensity.

institutions.name: The Broker's Desk
institutions.description: A cramped office at the back of the Exchange, walls covered in pinned contracts and route maps. Fernanda's desk is the cleanest surface — everything important is in her head.
institutions.function: Contract matching, market intelligence, trade opportunities. Better standing unlocks better contracts.
institutions.political_leaning: Pragmatic Alliance. Fernanda follows the rules — mostly — when it's profitable.

npcs.name: Vasco da Reira
npcs.title: Harbor Master
npcs.description: A lean man with ink-stained fingers and spectacles perched on a sharp nose. Vasco has logged every ship that entered Porto Novo for thirty-one years. He knows your tonnage before you drop anchor.
npcs.agenda: Order. Vasco wants every manifest filed, every fee collected, and every berth assigned by dawn. He despises smugglers, tolerates merchants, and respects captains who arrive with clean paperwork.
npcs.greeting_neutral: "Manifest and tonnage, Captain. I'll assign your berth once I've reviewed them."
npcs.greeting_friendly: "Ah, Captain — berth seven is clear. I saved it when I saw your sails. Your paperwork is always in order."
npcs.greeting_hostile: "Papers. Now. And if I find a single discrepancy, you'll wait in the outer harbor until I'm satisfied."
npcs.rumor: They say Vasco once held a merchant ship at anchor for three days because the manifest listed 'grain' instead of 'winter wheat.' The merchant never made the mistake again.

relationship_notes.pn_marta: Respects her. She keeps the Exchange running and that keeps his harbor orderly.
relationship_notes.pn_old_enzo: Wary. Enzo's tavern is where rules get bent. Vasco pretends not to notice.
relationship_notes.pn_senhora_costa: Defers to her completely. She appointed him. He serves her vision.
relationship_notes.pn_dimitri: Professional admiration. The shipyard runs clean — Vasco appreciates that.
relationship_notes.pn_inspector_salva: Allies. Salva enforces the law; Vasco enforces the paperwork. Two sides of the same coin.
relationship_notes.pn_broker_reis: Cordial. She needs his arrival logs; he appreciates her orderly contract paperwork.

npcs.name: Marta Soares
npcs.title: Guild Factor
npcs.description: Broad-shouldered, sharp-eyed, and always surrounded by three junior clerks trailing behind her with wax tablets. Marta is the Exchange Guild's chief factor — the woman who reads the dawn rates aloud from the Exchange steps every morning. She's never wrong about grain prices.
npcs.agenda: The Exchange Guild's dominance. Marta wants Porto Novo to remain the Mediterranean's price-setting authority. She views Al-Manar's Spice Circle as arrogant upstarts and Corsair's Rest as a stain on the region. She'll offer better rates to captains who bring grain and worse rates to anyone she suspects of dealing with the black market.
npcs.greeting_neutral: "You're here for the rates? They were posted at dawn. Grain is steady, spice is climbing. What are you buying?"
npcs.greeting_friendly: "Captain! Good timing — I have a surplus I need moved before the prices drop. Interested in a private arrangement?"
npcs.greeting_hostile: "I know where your last cargo came from. The Exchange remembers. Your rates will reflect that."
npcs.rumor: Marta once cornered the entire Mediterranean cotton market for three weeks. She bought everything, waited for the price to double, then sold. The Alliance pretended to disapprove. Secretly, they were impressed.

relationship_notes.pn_vasco: Uses him. Vasco's obsession with order serves the Guild perfectly.
relationship_notes.pn_old_enzo: Distrusts him deeply. Enzo's tavern is where black market contacts meet. She's sure of it but can't prove it.
relationship_notes.pn_senhora_costa: Rivals. Costa wants political stability; Marta wants market dominance. They clash on tariff policy monthly.
relationship_notes.pn_dimitri: Cordial. She needs his ships; he needs her contracts. Business.
relationship_notes.pn_inspector_salva: Values him. Salva catches the cheats she can't.

npcs.name: Dimitri Andros
npcs.title: Master Shipwright
npcs.description: Hands like ship timbers, salt-white beard, and a voice that carries across the entire yard. Dimitri has built more hulls than most captains have sailed. He judges a captain by the condition of their ship, not their silver. Bring him a well-maintained vessel and he'll work miracles. Bring him a wreck and he'll tell you what you did wrong — loudly.
npcs.agenda: The craft. Dimitri cares about ships, not politics. But he refuses to build warships for anyone — a principle that cost him the Iron Pact contract and earned him the Shipwrights' Brotherhood's eternal loyalty. He wants captains who respect their vessels.
npcs.greeting_neutral: "Let me see your hull before we talk price. I don't repair what I wouldn't sail."
npcs.greeting_friendly: "Captain! She's holding up well — you've been treating her right. Come, I have a new keel design to show you."
npcs.greeting_hostile: "What did you DO to this ship? This hull has been through a storm and a boarding and you didn't patch either. Get out of my yard until you learn to sail."
npcs.rumor: Dimitri was offered a fortune to build a flagship for the Crimson Tide. He told Scarlet Ana to build it herself. She laughed and left. They've been on oddly respectful terms ever since.

relationship_notes.pn_vasco: Gets along. Two professionals who understand duty.
relationship_notes.pn_marta: Tolerates. She's all about money; he's all about craft. Different species.
relationship_notes.pn_old_enzo: Drinking partners. Enzo's rum is the only thing that gets Dimitri off the yard after dark.
relationship_notes.pn_senhora_costa: Quiet loyalty. She protected the Brotherhood when the Iron Pact pressured them. He hasn't forgotten.
relationship_notes.pn_inspector_salva: Indifferent. Salva inspects cargo, not ships. Different jurisdictions.

npcs.name: Senhora Isabela Costa
npcs.title: Port Governor
npcs.description: Silver hair pulled back, always in a dark blue coat with the Exchange seal embroidered on the cuff. Senhora Costa has governed Porto Novo for twelve years — longer than any predecessor. She rules through consensus, which means she's always listening and never fully agreeing.
npcs.agenda: Stability and the Alliance. Costa wants Porto Novo prosperous, orderly, and at the center of Mediterranean trade. She views the Silk Circle's growing influence with concern and the Shadow Ports with outright hostility. She's the one who proposed the Alliance-wide weapons embargo against pirate-linked captains.
npcs.greeting_neutral: "Welcome to Porto Novo, Captain. I trust you'll find our markets fair and our laws clear."
npcs.greeting_friendly: "Captain — a pleasure. The Alliance benefits from captains of your standing. Will you join me for dinner? There are matters to discuss."
npcs.greeting_hostile: "Your reputation precedes you, Captain. I'll be candid: Porto Novo has standards. I suggest you meet them, or seek harbor elsewhere."
npcs.rumor: Costa was once a trader herself — ran the Al-Manar to Sun Harbor route for fifteen years before she entered politics. Some say she still keeps a ship hidden in Silva Bay, just in case.

relationship_notes.pn_vasco: Appointed him. He's her eyes on the harbor.
relationship_notes.pn_marta: Political rivals who need each other. Costa sets policy; Marta controls prices. Neither can rule alone.
relationship_notes.pn_old_enzo: Tolerates him. Enzo's tavern is useful — she gets intelligence from his rumors. He gets immunity from her inspectors.
relationship_notes.pn_dimitri: Protected his Brotherhood from the Iron Pact. He's quietly devoted.
relationship_notes.pn_inspector_salva: Her enforcer. Salva reports directly to her, not the Guild.

npcs.name: Old Enzo
npcs.title: Tavern Keeper
npcs.description: Round, red-faced, and always laughing at a joke only he heard. Old Enzo has run the Harbor Bell tavern since before Vasco started keeping records. He knows everyone's secrets and tells none of them — unless the rum is good enough and the listener is interesting enough.
npcs.agenda: Survival and stories. Enzo is the unofficial bridge between Porto Novo's legitimate world and its shadow. He doesn't smuggle — but he knows who does. He doesn't break laws — but he bends them into pretzels. His tavern is where contracts are whispered before they're signed, where crew is recruited, and where captains learn which routes are safe this season.
npcs.greeting_neutral: "Sit! Drink! You look like a captain who's been at sea too long. First one's on the house — I'll put it on your next cargo."
npcs.greeting_friendly: "My favorite captain! Your usual table is waiting. I may have heard something that interests you — but first, how was the voyage?"
npcs.greeting_hostile: "...Ah. You. The rum is full-price tonight, and I haven't heard any rumors. Strange, isn't it? Usually I hear everything."
npcs.rumor: Old Enzo was a pirate once — or so the story goes. He never confirms and never denies. His left hand is missing two fingers, and he changes the subject if you ask about them.

relationship_notes.pn_vasco: Amused by him. Vasco pretends the tavern doesn't exist. Enzo finds this hilarious.
relationship_notes.pn_marta: Wary. Marta suspects him of facilitating black market deals. She's not entirely wrong.
relationship_notes.pn_dimitri: Best friends. They drink together every night and argue about ships vs. rum. Neither wins.
relationship_notes.pn_senhora_costa: Useful to each other. She gets intelligence; he gets protection. An unspoken deal that works.
relationship_notes.pn_inspector_salva: Keeps his distance. Salva is the one person in Porto Novo that Enzo genuinely fears.

npcs.name: Inspector Salva
npcs.title: Chief Customs Inspector
npcs.description: Thin as a blade, with eyes that miss nothing and a memory for cargo that borders on supernatural. Inspector Salva has never accepted a bribe — not because he's incorruptible, but because the satisfaction of catching a smuggler is worth more to him than silver.
npcs.agenda: The law. Salva is Senhora Costa's instrument, but his motivation is personal. His brother was killed by black powder smuggled through a legitimate port. Every contraband seizure is a small act of justice. He is thorough, fair, and absolutely merciless with anyone carrying undeclared goods.
npcs.greeting_neutral: "Cargo manifest. All of it. I'll inspect the hold at my discretion."
npcs.greeting_friendly: "Captain. Your record is clean — I appreciate that more than you know. Standard inspection, quick and painless."
npcs.greeting_hostile: "Open every hold. Every crate. Every barrel. I have all day, Captain. Do you?"
npcs.rumor: Salva once inspected a ship for nine hours straight. Found three false panels, a hidden compartment, and enough opium to fill a rowboat. The captain is still in prison.

relationship_notes.pn_vasco: Allies. Vasco's paperwork makes Salva's job easier.
relationship_notes.pn_marta: Professional respect. She wants cheats caught; he catches them.
relationship_notes.pn_senhora_costa: Reports to her. Loyal, but his real loyalty is to the law itself.
relationship_notes.pn_old_enzo: The one Enzo fears. Salva suspects the tavern is a contact point. He hasn't proven it yet. Yet.

npcs.name: Fernanda Reis
npcs.title: Senior Broker
npcs.description: Dark eyes, quick hands, and a mind that tracks six contracts simultaneously without writing anything down. Fernanda runs the broker's desk at the Exchange — the place where contracts are matched to captains and opportunities become obligations.
npcs.agenda: Commission and connections. Fernanda takes a cut of every contract she brokers. She wants high-value captains who complete deliveries on time, because their success is her reputation. She'll steer good contracts toward reliable captains and leave the scraps for unknowns.
npcs.greeting_neutral: "New captain? I have contracts. Small ones, for now. Complete them on time and we'll talk about the real work."
npcs.greeting_friendly: "Captain! I've been holding something for you — a charter that requires someone I trust. Interested?"
npcs.greeting_hostile: "I have nothing for you today. Or tomorrow. Come back when your reputation improves — if it can."
npcs.rumor: Fernanda once brokered a grain contract worth more than the entire port's weekly revenue. The captain delivered early. Fernanda bought a house. They're still partners.

relationship_notes.pn_vasco: Cordial. She needs his arrival logs to time her offers.
relationship_notes.pn_marta: Complex. The Guild sets the rates; Fernanda sets the contracts. They compete for influence over trade flow.
relationship_notes.pn_senhora_costa: Costa approves her contracts. Fernanda makes sure the right ones cross Costa's desk.
relationship_notes.pn_old_enzo: Useful. Enzo's tavern rumors tell her which captains are desperate — desperation makes captains take risky contracts.
relationship_notes.pn_inspector_salva: Careful around him. Some of her contracts brush close to grey areas. Salva doesn't need to know.

port_institutions.power_structure: Al-Manar is governed by hereditary merchant aristocracy — the Khoury family has held the title 'Merchant Princess' for six generations. But real power is shared: Nadia sets policy, Yasmin controls the spice market through the Circle, and Hakim's apothecary gives Al-Manar a unique trade advantage. Old Farouk's tea house is where all three go to think — separately, each believing they're unobserved. Zara, poached from Porto Novo, protects the market's integrity. Tariq pushes for expansion at the broker's desk, supported by Nadia but watched by everyone.
port_institutions.internal_tension: The core tension is between tradition and ambition. Yasmin wants to preserve Al-Manar's ancient way — the Bazaar's authority, the Circle's traditions, the slow pace of tea-and-negotiation commerce. Tariq wants to modernize — faster contracts, direct Silk Circle partnerships, bypassing Porto Novo entirely. Nadia is playing both sides: she funds Tariq's ambitions while publicly deferring to Yasmin's traditions. Meanwhile, Nadia's private correspondence with the Silk Circle could reshape the entire Alliance — or destroy it. Only Farouk suspects the full picture, and he's not talking.

institutions.name: The Harbor of Arrivals
institutions.description: A curved stone quay lined with date palms, with a reception pavilion where arriving captains are offered dates and water before any business is discussed. The harbor is smaller than Porto Novo's but immaculately maintained. Every bollard is polished bronze.
institutions.function: Controls docking, assigns berths, collects port fees. Arrival is a ceremony here, not a transaction.
institutions.political_leaning: Alliance loyalist with Al-Manar pride. Khalil serves the city's dignity before the Alliance's efficiency.

institutions.name: The Spice Bazaar
institutions.description: A covered market stretching three city blocks, its ceiling hung with brass lamps and dried herb bundles. A hundred stalls compete for the nose — cinnamon, cardamom, saffron, clove. The auction floor is at the center, where the Spice Mother holds court every morning.
institutions.function: Sets spice prices, auctions rare lots, arbitrates quality disputes. The Mediterranean's premier spice market.
institutions.political_leaning: Al-Manar supremacist. The Bazaar believes it IS Mediterranean trade, and Porto Novo is just a granary.

institutions.name: The Khoury Palace
institutions.description: A tiled palace above the harbor where every surface catches light — mosaics of trade ships, courtyards with fountains, and a receiving room where the Merchant Princess conducts business from a divan instead of a desk. Six generations of Khourys watch from portraits on the walls.
institutions.function: Sets port policy, manages diplomatic relations, controls the port treasury. Hereditary governance — not elected.
institutions.political_leaning: Alliance member with independent ambitions. Nadia is loyal to the Alliance when it serves Al-Manar, and creative when it doesn't.

institutions.name: The Amber Glass
institutions.description: Not a tavern — a tea house. Low tables, silk cushions, and the quiet murmur of conversation conducted in a language that rum drinkers wouldn't understand. The amber glass windows filter the harbor light into gold. Everything here moves at the speed of tea.
institutions.function: Social hub, intelligence exchange, crew recruitment. Information flows over tea, not rum. Deals are conceived here before they're signed anywhere else.
institutions.political_leaning: Neutral, but Farouk's neutrality is informed. He knows everything and judges nothing — which makes him invaluable to everyone.

institutions.name: The Scales of Truth
institutions.description: A marble building with the inscription 'WEIGHT AND TRUTH' carved above the door. Inside, brass scales of extraordinary precision line the walls. Zara's office is spare — a desk, a lamp, and a collection of confiscated counterfeit spices mounted in glass cases like specimens.
institutions.function: Cargo inspection focused on QUALITY and AUTHENTICITY, not just legality. Fake saffron is a worse crime than smuggling here.
institutions.political_leaning: Quality enforcement. Zara serves Al-Manar's reputation, which happens to align with Alliance standards.

institutions.name: The Apothecary House
institutions.description: A whitewashed building with a garden of medicinal herbs on the roof. Inside, the air is thick with eucalyptus and camphor. Shelves of labeled jars line every wall — roots, dried flowers, mineral powders, pressed oils. Hakim's workbench is at the center, surrounded by mortars and handwritten recipe books.
institutions.function: Medicine production, quality certification, medicinal ingredient trading. Unique to Al-Manar — no other port has a dedicated apothecary institution.
institutions.political_leaning: Humanitarian. Hakim serves health, not politics. But his medicines give Al-Manar a trade advantage nobody talks about openly.

institutions.name: The Broker's Alcove
institutions.description: An arched alcove off the Bazaar's main hall, curtained with silk — because in Al-Manar, even contract negotiations happen behind beautiful fabric. Tariq's desk is polished rosewood. The contracts on it are handwritten on parchment, not printed on paper like Porto Novo's.
institutions.function: Contract matching with an emphasis on prestige and exclusivity. Better contracts than Porto Novo — but fewer of them, and you have to earn access.
institutions.political_leaning: Ambitious Al-Manar loyalist. Tariq wants the Alcove to replace Porto Novo's desk as the Alliance's contract center.

npcs.name: Khalil al-Rashid
npcs.title: Harbor Master
npcs.description: A tall man in white robes with a gold chain of office that he wears even in the sweltering heat. Khalil treats every arriving ship as a diplomatic event. He greets captains personally, offers dates and water, and only then asks for paperwork. The ceremony is the paperwork.
npcs.agenda: Dignity. Khalil believes Al-Manar's harbor should reflect the city's ancient prestige. He wants captains to feel honored to dock here — and to pay accordingly. He quietly resents Porto Novo's larger harbor and compensates with superior hospitality.
npcs.greeting_neutral: "Welcome to Al-Manar, Captain. Please — dates, water. We discuss your berth after you have rested from the sea."
npcs.greeting_friendly: "Captain! The harbor sings your name. Your berth awaits, and I have taken the liberty of arranging fresh provisions. We are honored."
npcs.greeting_hostile: "...Captain. You may dock at the outer quay. The inner harbor is reserved for merchants of established reputation."
npcs.rumor: Khalil once refused docking to a Porto Novo flagship because the captain didn't observe the greeting ritual. The diplomatic incident lasted a month. Khalil didn't apologize.

relationship_notes.am_yasmin: Deep respect. The Spice Mother is the heart of the city. He serves her vision.
relationship_notes.am_old_farouk: Fond. Farouk's tea house is where Khalil relaxes — the only place he drops the ceremony.
relationship_notes.am_senhora_nadia: Loyal. She appointed him. He repays that trust with flawless protocol.
relationship_notes.am_inspector_zara: Uneasy. Zara's inspections sometimes lack the grace Khalil expects. Efficiency without elegance offends him.
relationship_notes.am_hakim: Respectful. The Apothecary Master's medicines are part of Al-Manar's prestige.
relationship_notes.am_broker_tariq: Cordial. Tariq brings quality captains. Quality captains deserve quality arrivals.

npcs.name: Yasmin al-Nadir
npcs.title: The Spice Mother
npcs.description: Silver rings on every finger, robes that smell of cardamom and saffron, and eyes that have judged the quality of spice for fifty years. Yasmin is the Spice Merchants' Circle's eldest — they call her the Spice Mother. She doesn't negotiate. She declares the price, and the market adjusts.
npcs.agenda: Al-Manar's supremacy. Yasmin believes Al-Manar — not Porto Novo — is the true heart of Mediterranean trade. Grain is survival; spice is civilization. She wants the Spice Circle to lead the Exchange Alliance, and she'll use every trade relationship, every favor owed, and every ounce of her considerable influence to make it happen.
npcs.greeting_neutral: "You come to the Bazaar? Good. Tell me what you carry, and I will tell you what it is worth. In Al-Manar, the price is the truth."
npcs.greeting_friendly: "Ah, a captain who understands quality. Come — I have set aside a blend that even my daughters haven't tasted. For trusted friends only."
npcs.greeting_hostile: "I know what you've been trading. And where. The Bazaar has long memories, Captain. Your prices here will reflect that."
npcs.rumor: Yasmin once tasted a spice blend and named the island it came from, the year of harvest, and the family who grew it. She was right on all three counts. Nobody tests her anymore.

relationship_notes.am_khalil: Appreciates his ceremony. It reflects Al-Manar's dignity — which is her life's work.
relationship_notes.am_old_farouk: Her oldest friend. They've argued about spice and tea for forty years. Neither has conceded a single point.
relationship_notes.am_senhora_nadia: Political ally, personal rival. Both want Al-Manar to lead. They disagree on how.
relationship_notes.am_inspector_zara: Useful. Zara catches the counterfeit spice that Yasmin's reputation can't afford.
relationship_notes.am_hakim: Family. Hakim is her nephew. She appointed him. His success is her legacy.
relationship_notes.am_broker_tariq: Watches him carefully. Tariq is ambitious. Ambition is useful — until it isn't.

npcs.name: Senhora Nadia Khoury
npcs.title: Merchant Princess
npcs.description: Dark eyes, impeccable posture, and the quiet authority of someone who has never had to raise her voice to be obeyed. Nadia's family has governed Al-Manar for six generations — she inherited the title 'Merchant Princess' along with the port's debts and ambitions. She governs from a tiled palace above the harbor, where every surface reflects light.
npcs.agenda: Legacy. Nadia wants Al-Manar to outlast her — to be the port her great-grandchildren govern. She's more patient than Costa, more political than Marta, and more dangerous than either because she thinks in generations, not quarters. She's been quietly building trade relationships with the Silk Circle — something the Alliance would consider dangerously close to disloyalty.
npcs.greeting_neutral: "Al-Manar welcomes all who trade with honor. My house is open, Captain. What brings you to our harbor?"
npcs.greeting_friendly: "Captain — you honor my house with your return. I have been thinking about our last conversation. There is an opportunity I wish to discuss."
npcs.greeting_hostile: "My harbor master informs me of your... recent activities. I will be plain: Al-Manar remembers everything. Consider your next trade carefully."
npcs.rumor: Nadia has been exchanging private letters with a Silk Circle official. The Alliance doesn't know — or pretends not to. If it's a trade deal, it could reshape Mediterranean commerce. If it's betrayal, it could shatter the Alliance.

relationship_notes.am_khalil: Her appointee. His ceremony reflects her standards.
relationship_notes.am_yasmin: Political ally, personal rival. Yasmin wants the Circle to lead; Nadia wants the Khoury family to lead. Both want Al-Manar on top.
relationship_notes.am_old_farouk: Amused by him. His tea house is where she goes to think without being watched — or so she believes.
relationship_notes.am_inspector_zara: Respects her competence. Zara is the best inspector in the Mediterranean. Nadia poached her from Porto Novo.
relationship_notes.am_hakim: Patron. She funds his apothecary research from the port treasury. His medicines are Al-Manar's quiet advantage.
relationship_notes.am_broker_tariq: Grooming him. Tariq is young, sharp, and loyal — for now. She's testing whether he stays loyal when the stakes rise.

npcs.name: Old Farouk
npcs.title: Tea Master
npcs.description: Weathered face, calm hands, and the patience of a man who has brewed ten thousand pots of tea and plans to brew ten thousand more. Old Farouk runs the Amber Glass — not a tavern but a tea house, because in Al-Manar, information flows over tea, not rum. He listens more than he speaks, and what he speaks is worth the silence.
npcs.agenda: Understanding. Farouk doesn't want power or silver — he wants to understand why people trade, why they sail, why they risk everything for cargo that could sink in a storm. He collects stories the way Yasmin collects spices. His tea house is where captains come to think, and where deals are conceived before anyone signs anything.
npcs.greeting_neutral: "Sit. Tea first. Business is for those who have already tasted patience."
npcs.greeting_friendly: "My friend — the good leaves today. I saved them when I heard your ship on the horizon. Tell me: what did the sea teach you this time?"
npcs.greeting_hostile: "...Tea is served to all. Even those the harbor distrusts. Sit, if you wish. But the good leaves are not for everyone."
npcs.rumor: Farouk was a navigator once — sailed the Monsoon Shortcut seven times. He retired after the seventh, saying he'd learned everything the sea had to teach. Nobody knows if he meant the route or something else entirely.

relationship_notes.am_khalil: The only person who sees Khalil without the ceremony. They play chess in the evenings.
relationship_notes.am_yasmin: Forty years of argument about whether spice or tea is the higher art. The argument IS the friendship.
relationship_notes.am_senhora_nadia: She comes to his tea house to think. He lets her believe she's not being observed.
relationship_notes.am_inspector_zara: Sympathetic. Zara carries a weight Farouk recognizes. He serves her a special blend — calming, no charge.
relationship_notes.am_hakim: Mentored him as a boy. Taught Hakim that medicine is patience, not ingredients.
relationship_notes.am_broker_tariq: Wary. Tariq moves too fast. Farouk has seen what happens to men who outrun their wisdom.

npcs.name: Inspector Zara Osman
npcs.title: Chief Customs Inspector
npcs.description: Short hair, sharp uniform, and the focused intensity of a surgeon. Zara was Porto Novo's best inspector before Nadia poached her with a better title and a harder challenge: Al-Manar's spice market attracts the most sophisticated counterfeiters in the Mediterranean. Zara can identify fake saffron by smell alone.
npcs.agenda: Authenticity. Zara's mission is protecting Al-Manar's reputation for quality. Counterfeit spice dilutes the market and destroys trust. She cares less about smuggling than about fraud — a captain carrying real goods gets a nod; a captain carrying adulterated spice gets a cell. She misses Porto Novo sometimes. Salva was a good partner.
npcs.greeting_neutral: "Cargo for inspection. I'm particularly interested in your spice lots — origin documentation, please."
npcs.greeting_friendly: "Captain — your goods are always genuine. Quick inspection, and you're through. I wish every captain traded as cleanly."
npcs.greeting_hostile: "Open everything. I've seen cargo from your route before, Captain, and I've found problems. Let's see if today is different."
npcs.rumor: Zara left Porto Novo after a disagreement with Inspector Salva about methods. Salva hunts smugglers; Zara hunts frauds. They respect each other but couldn't work together. Different obsessions.

relationship_notes.am_khalil: Tolerates his ceremony. She'd prefer efficiency, but his greeting ritual gives her time to observe the crew.
relationship_notes.am_yasmin: Allies. Yasmin's reputation depends on quality. Zara guarantees it.
relationship_notes.am_senhora_nadia: Loyal. Nadia gave her the freedom Salva wouldn't. In return, Zara protects Al-Manar's market integrity.
relationship_notes.am_old_farouk: Grateful. Farouk's tea is the only thing that helps her sleep. The job wears on her.
relationship_notes.am_hakim: Professional respect. His medicines are always pure. She never needs to inspect twice.
relationship_notes.am_broker_tariq: Watching him. Some of Tariq's contracts originate from sources she hasn't verified. That bothers her.

npcs.name: Hakim al-Nadir
npcs.title: Apothecary Master
npcs.description: Soft-spoken, always smelling faintly of eucalyptus, with ink-stained fingers from recording recipes. Hakim is Yasmin's nephew — he inherited her nose for quality but not her ruthlessness. He runs Al-Manar's Apothecary Guild, blending medicines from spice-market ingredients that no other port can replicate.
npcs.agenda: Healing. Hakim genuinely wants to cure sickness, not profit from it. He sells medicines at fair prices — which infuriates merchants who want to mark them up. He's building a collection of medicinal recipes from every region, and he'll trade generously with any captain who brings him ingredients from the East Indies or South Seas.
npcs.greeting_neutral: "Captain — do you carry medicines or ingredients? I'm always interested in what the sea brings. And if you need healing, my rates are fair."
npcs.greeting_friendly: "My friend! Did you find the root I asked about? No? No matter — come, see what I've been working on. I think I've cracked the Ember Isle formula."
npcs.greeting_hostile: "I heal all who ask. That is my oath. But I will not supply medicines for... questionable purposes. If your intentions are honest, I am here."
npcs.rumor: Hakim turned down a fortune from the Iron Pact for exclusive medicine rights. He said healing belongs to everyone, not to the highest bidder. Yasmin was furious. Then she was proud.

relationship_notes.am_khalil: Grateful. Khalil ensures medicine shipments get priority berthing.
relationship_notes.am_yasmin: His aunt, his patron, his harshest critic. She expects perfection. He tries to give her compassion instead.
relationship_notes.am_senhora_nadia: His patron from the treasury. She funds his research. He's not sure why — political advantage or genuine interest. Both, probably.
relationship_notes.am_old_farouk: His mentor. Farouk taught him patience. Every recipe begins with patience.
relationship_notes.am_inspector_zara: Grateful she's here. Counterfeit medicines kill people. Zara stops counterfeits.
relationship_notes.am_broker_tariq: Uneasy. Tariq keeps suggesting he should raise his prices. Hakim keeps refusing.

npcs.name: Tariq Sayed
npcs.title: Senior Broker
npcs.description: Young, sharp-dressed, and always moving. Tariq is the youngest senior broker in Al-Manar's history — appointed by Nadia over the objections of older candidates. He has excellent instincts for matching captains to contracts, but his ambition makes the establishment nervous. He wants Al-Manar's broker desk to rival Porto Novo's, and he's not patient about it.
npcs.agenda: Prominence. Tariq wants to make Al-Manar the contract capital of the Mediterranean — not just the spice capital. He's been quietly courting Silk Circle traders for exclusive luxury contracts that bypass Porto Novo entirely. If he succeeds, it shifts the balance of power within the Alliance. If he fails, Nadia will deny she ever supported him.
npcs.greeting_neutral: "Captain. I have contracts — good ones. Al-Manar doesn't waste time with small work. Tell me your capacity and I'll match you."
npcs.greeting_friendly: "Captain! I've been waiting for you. I have something — a contract that Fernanda in Porto Novo would kill for. But it came to MY desk first."
npcs.greeting_hostile: "I... don't have anything suitable for your profile at this time. Perhaps try Porto Novo? I hear their standards are more... flexible."
npcs.rumor: Tariq was seen dining with a Silk Circle merchant from Jade Port. If he's brokering a direct Al-Manar-to-Jade-Port luxury contract, it would be the biggest deal in a decade — and Porto Novo's Fernanda Reis would be furious.

relationship_notes.am_khalil: Impatient with the ceremony but respects its purpose. First impressions matter for contract negotiations.
relationship_notes.am_yasmin: She watches him. He knows she watches him. He performs for her judgment while trying to exceed it.
relationship_notes.am_senhora_nadia: His patron. She appointed him. He suspects she's testing him. He's right.
relationship_notes.am_old_farouk: Avoids the tea house. Farouk sees through him, and Tariq isn't ready to be seen through yet.
relationship_notes.am_inspector_zara: Careful. Some of his contracts push boundaries. Zara hasn't said anything — yet.
relationship_notes.am_hakim: Frustrated. Hakim's medicines could be worth a fortune if he'd just raise his prices. Hakim won't. Tariq finds this baffling.

port_institutions.power_structure: Silva Bay is a shipwrights' republic — no single ruler, no hereditary title. The Brotherhood Council of seven governs by consensus, chaired by the elected Master Shipwright (Elena). The yard IS the town: Elena builds the ships, Tomás grades the timber, Nuno runs the harbor, and everything else exists to support that work. Rosa's tavern is the unofficial second chamber where real opinions emerge. Ana's broker bench funds it all. Pires, the Alliance customs officer, is tolerated but never included.
port_institutions.internal_tension: The core tension is independence vs. relevance. The Brotherhood governs itself and answers to no one — but the Alliance provides trade protection and market access that Silva Bay needs. Elena wants to stay free; the Alliance wants Silva Bay's ships. The leverage is mutual, which creates a fragile equilibrium. Tomás adds a second tension: his harvest limits protect the forests but frustrate merchants who want more timber faster. The quiet tension is Pires — an outsider who represents everything the Brotherhood distrusts (external authority), yet who genuinely tries to belong. Ana is his only ally, and she's still earning her own place.

institutions.name: The Master Shipyard
institutions.description: The largest shipyard in the Mediterranean — three slipways, two dry docks, a steam box for bending timber, and a mast pond where logs season for years before they're touched. The sign over the gate reads 'BUILT TO SAIL, NOT TO SINK.' It's not a motto. It's a threat.
institutions.function: Ship repairs, upgrades, and purchases. The best work in the game — cheapest repairs (1 silver/hull point). Elena's standards are the price of admission.
institutions.political_leaning: Apolitical. The yard builds for anyone. ANYONE. Except warmongers.

institutions.name: The Working Harbor
institutions.description: No ceremony, no pavilion — just a clipboard, a tide table nailed to a post, and Nuno squinting at your approach. Timber barges have priority; everyone else fits where they fit. The harbor smells of fresh-cut wood and pitch.
institutions.function: Berth assignment, timber logistics. No ceremony — function over form. Nuno runs it like a shipwright runs a project.
institutions.political_leaning: Brotherhood-aligned. The harbor serves the yard first, everything else second.

institutions.name: The Timber Yard
institutions.description: An open-air grading yard where logs are stacked by species, quality, and seasoning time. No building — just canopies for rain and Tomás with his grading chalk. Every log gets a mark: A for hull-grade, B for general, C for firewood. There is no D. If it's worse than C, it goes back.
institutions.function: Timber grading, pricing, and sales. Not an auction — prices are set by quality grade. Fair, transparent, no haggling.
institutions.political_leaning: Conservation-minded. Tomás limits harvests to protect forests. Unpopular with volume buyers.

institutions.name: The Brotherhood Hall
institutions.description: A timber longhouse with walls carved with the names of every ship built in Silva Bay for two hundred years. Seven chairs around a round table — no head seat, because the Brotherhood governs as equals. A ship's bell hangs from the ceiling, rung to open and close each session.
institutions.function: Self-governance by council of seven shipwrights. No external authority. Alliance membership is by choice, not obligation.
institutions.political_leaning: Fiercely independent. Alliance membership is conditional — cross the Brotherhood's principles and they leave.

institutions.name: The Dry Dock
institutions.description: Built from the timbers of a decommissioned brigantine — the bar is the original helm, and the booths are made from hull sections. Sawdust on the floor, ship models on every shelf, and the sound of the yard leaking in through walls that were never meant to be walls. The fish stew is legendary. The sawdust content is debatable.
institutions.function: Social hub, crew recruitment, unofficial council annex. Where Silva Bay actually makes decisions.
institutions.political_leaning: Community heart. Rosa doesn't take sides — but her tavern is where sides are chosen.

institutions.name: The Customs Shed
institutions.description: A wooden shed at the edge of the dock — the most modest customs office in the Mediterranean. A desk, a chair, a stamp, and a young man who wishes he were somewhere else. The shed leaks when it rains. Nobody has offered to fix it.
institutions.function: Minimal cargo inspection. Alliance requirement, not Brotherhood priority. Quick and apologetic.
institutions.political_leaning: Alliance outsider. Pires represents Porto Novo's rules in a town that makes its own.

institutions.name: The Broker's Bench
