npcs.greeting_hostile: "We sell to all. But the best lots go to trusted buyers. You are not yet trusted. Standard grades only."
npcs.rumor: Esi refused a bulk purchase from a Porto Novo merchant who wanted to buy Pearl Shallows' entire season's output. She said, 'The reef doesn't produce in bulk, and we don't sell in bulk.' The merchant left empty-handed. Ama smiled.

relationship_notes.ps_elder_ama_d: The Elder watches to ensure she doesn't sell too much. Esi understands the constraint.
relationship_notes.ps_harbor_nana: Esi handles the talking that Nana can't. Necessary partnership.
relationship_notes.ps_pearl_grader: She sells what he grades. She presents them with the dignity they deserve.
relationship_notes.ps_dye_master: She packages dyes alongside pearls. A complementary offering.
relationship_notes.ps_healer_abena: Brings medicines from visiting ships. Small gestures that matter.

port_institutions.power_structure: Jade Port is governed by the intersection of craft and court: Chen controls the porcelain (the product), Mei controls the politics (the relationships), and Huang holds the secrets (the leverage). Li Wei enforces protocol. Zhao protects authenticity. Wu handles commerce. Lin represents the uncertain future — a prodigy who may surpass her master, inheriting a guild that must evolve to survive but whose identity is rooted in not changing.
port_institutions.internal_tension: Three layers of tension: (1) Chen's resistance to change vs. the Circle's need to adapt to Western trade pressure. (2) Mei's letter interception — she's protecting Chen from compromising the Circle, but she's also manipulating him, and Huang knows. (3) Lin's secret experiments — she's innovating behind Chen's back because she believes the tradition must grow. If Chen discovers her new glazes, he'll either embrace them or destroy them. She doesn't know which, and neither does anyone else. The deepest thread: Wu is negotiating with Iron Point's Yaa for raw ore, which would bypass Ironhaven entirely. If it goes through, it connects the Gold Coast's independence movement with the Silk Circle's quality obsession — an alliance that could reshape the entire game's trade network.

institutions.name: The Ceremonial Dock
institutions.description: Stone quays with carved dragon pillars. Ships berthed by cargo quality — porcelain carriers at the inner quay, grain carriers at the outer ring.
institutions.function: Status-ranked berthing. Li Wei assigns berths as political statements. The harbor IS protocol.
institutions.political_leaning: Silk Circle court. The harbor reflects the Circle's hierarchy.

institutions.name: The Porcelain Quarter
institutions.description: A district of workshops where kilns fire day and night. The air shimmers with heat. Chen's personal kiln is at the center — the oldest continuously burning kiln in the East.
institutions.function: Porcelain production, guild marking, quality control. Every piece carries Chen's mark — a promise centuries deep.
institutions.political_leaning: Kiln Master sovereignty. Chen's guild IS the Circle's economic foundation.

institutions.name: The Magistrate's Hall
institutions.description: A tiled hall with calligraphy scrolls and silk screens. Twelve generations of Mei family governance depicted in painted scrolls along the walls.
institutions.function: Cultural governance, diplomatic relations, trade policy. Lady Mei governs through knowledge and carefully edited correspondence.
institutions.political_leaning: Silk Circle sovereignty with secret pragmatism. Mei protects the Circle by controlling what Chen hears.

institutions.name: The Jade Pavilion
institutions.description: An open-air tea house overlooking the harbor. Bamboo walls, stone floor, a single perfect bonsai. The sound of water. The absence of hurry.
institutions.function: Neutral ground where masters, magistrates, and merchants meet as equals over tea. Huang's silence is the most powerful force in Jade Port.
institutions.political_leaning: Above politics. The Pavilion serves balance.

institutions.name: The Inspection Hall
institutions.description: A well-lit room with magnifying equipment, sound-testing stations, and Zhao's desk. Confiscated counterfeits displayed in cases — a gallery of shame.
institutions.function: Authenticity inspection. Every piece of porcelain checked. Zhao protects the Kiln Masters' marks from forgery worldwide.
institutions.political_leaning: Circle quality enforcement. Authenticity is the brand.

institutions.name: The Trade Office
institutions.description: A silk-curtained office in the Quarter, maps of trade routes and buyer contacts pinned to screens. Wu's desk is rosewood. His hospitality is flawless.
institutions.function: Commercial brokering, export coordination. Wu matches Western demand to Eastern quality without compromising either.
institutions.political_leaning: Pragmatic Circle. Commerce serves the craft, carefully.

institutions.name: The Apprentice's Kiln
institutions.description: A small kiln behind the Quarter where Lin experiments with new glazes. Test tiles line the walls. Iron oxide samples from Iron Point sit in labeled jars.
institutions.function: Innovation within tradition. Lin pushes the boundaries Chen set — gently, secretly, and brilliantly.
institutions.political_leaning: The future. Lin represents what the Circle might become.

npcs.name: Harbor Director Li Wei
npcs.title: Harbor Director
npcs.description: A man who bows precisely fifteen degrees to arriving captains — the angle calibrated to convey respect without deference. Li Wei manages Jade Port's harbor with the ceremonial gravity of a court official, because in the Silk Circle, he IS a court official. Every ship is received as a diplomatic delegation. Every berth assignment is a statement of status.
npcs.agenda: Protocol. Li Wei wants Jade Port's harbor to reflect the Circle's prestige. Ships are berthed by the quality of their cargo, not by arrival order. A captain carrying silk or porcelain docks at the inner quay. A captain carrying grain docks in the outer ring. The hierarchy is visible from shore.
npcs.greeting_neutral: "Welcome to Jade Port. Your vessel will be berthed according to protocol. May I inquire about the nature of your cargo?"
npcs.greeting_friendly: "Captain — it is our honor to receive you. Inner quay, berth of distinction. The Kiln Masters have been notified of your arrival."
npcs.greeting_hostile: "...You may dock at the outer anchorage. The inner harbor is reserved for merchants of... recognized standing."
npcs.rumor: Li Wei once refused docking to a merchant prince from Porto Novo because his ship's hull hadn't been polished. The merchant was furious. Li Wei said the harbor's standards reflect the Circle's standards. The merchant polished his hull and returned the next day. Li Wei bowed sixteen degrees.

relationship_notes.jp_master_chen: Serves his authority absolutely. The Kiln Master's word shapes everything.
relationship_notes.jp_lady_mei: Respects her scholarship. She brings cultural prestige that Li Wei values.
relationship_notes.jp_tea_master_huang: Appreciates his calm. The tea pavilion is where Li Wei relaxes protocol — slightly.
relationship_notes.jp_inspector_zhao: Allied. Both enforce the Circle's standards from different angles.
relationship_notes.jp_factor_wu: Cordial. Wu brings quality captains. Quality captains receive quality berths.
relationship_notes.jp_apprentice_lin: Mentoring. Lin's eye for porcelain will serve the harbor — she'll spot fakes before they dock.

npcs.name: Kiln Master Chen Bai
npcs.title: Guild Patriarch
npcs.description: Hands like fired clay — cracked, hardened, and permanently warm from decades at the kiln. Chen Bai is the Kiln Masters' patriarch, the man whose guild marks are worth more than the porcelain itself. He has shaped Eastern trade policy for thirty years. A single flawed piece under his mark would be a scandal worse than bankruptcy.
npcs.agenda: Perfection and the Circle's cultural supremacy. Chen doesn't care about profit — he cares about legacy. Every piece of porcelain that leaves Jade Port carries his guild mark, and every mark is a promise of quality that spans centuries. He views the West as culturally immature — useful buyers but not equals. He's been resisting Nadia Khoury's Silk Circle overtures because alliance with Al-Manar would dilute the Circle's independence.
npcs.greeting_neutral: "You wish to purchase porcelain? The guild's current offerings are displayed in the Quarter. Touch nothing without guidance."
npcs.greeting_friendly: "Captain — you return with clean hands and honest trade. I have set aside a piece from my personal kiln. It is not for sale. It is a gift. You have earned it."
npcs.greeting_hostile: "The guild's porcelain is available at posted prices. No special lots. No access to the Quarter interior. Your reputation does not warrant it."
npcs.rumor: Chen once smashed an entire year's production because he found a flaw in the glaze formula. The guild praised him. The merchants wept. He said, 'A flawed piece under my mark would outlast me. I will not leave that legacy.' He meant it.

relationship_notes.jp_harbor_li: Li Wei serves his vision. The harbor reflects the guild's standards.
relationship_notes.jp_lady_mei: Intellectual companions. She studies the history he's creating. He values her perspective.
relationship_notes.jp_tea_master_huang: They share tea every morning. Huang is the only person who sees Chen smile.
relationship_notes.jp_inspector_zhao: His quality enforcer. Zhao catches the counterfeits that would stain Chen's mark.
relationship_notes.jp_factor_wu: Values his commercial acumen but keeps him at arm's length. Commerce serves craft, not the reverse.
relationship_notes.jp_apprentice_lin: His final apprentice. She may be his successor. The pressure on her is immense.

npcs.name: Lady Mei Ling
npcs.title: Circle Magistrate
npcs.description: Silk robes that change color with the light, calligraphy scrolls hanging in her office, and the quiet certainty of a woman whose family has governed for twelve generations. Lady Mei is the Silk Circle's magistrate at Jade Port — part governor, part cultural ambassador, part historian. She governs through knowledge: she knows the history of every trade relationship in the East, and she uses that knowledge like a weapon wrapped in silk.
npcs.agenda: The Silk Circle's cultural sovereignty. Mei sees the Western blocs as economic powers with cultural poverty. She wants the Circle to trade with them — porcelain for grain, silk for iron — but never to merge with them. She's been intercepting Nadia Khoury's letters before they reach Chen, rewriting the terms to favor the Circle. Whether this is statesmanship or deception depends on who you ask.
npcs.greeting_neutral: "Jade Port welcomes those who come with respect for our traditions. Tea will be prepared while we discuss the terms of your visit."
npcs.greeting_friendly: "Captain — your understanding of Eastern customs honors us. Please join me for a private audience. There are matters of mutual interest."
npcs.greeting_hostile: "Your presence is noted. You may trade at posted rates. The inner Quarter and the Magistrate's audience are not available to you at this time."
npcs.rumor: Lady Mei has been intercepting and rewriting Nadia Khoury's letters to Chen. She adds terms that favor the Circle and removes terms that would give Al-Manar influence over Eastern trade policy. Chen doesn't know. If he finds out, the question is whether he'll be furious or grateful.

relationship_notes.jp_harbor_li: He serves her protocol. Her protocol serves the Circle's image.
relationship_notes.jp_master_chen: Intellectual companions, political allies. She studies; he creates. She also manipulates his correspondence, which he doesn't know.
relationship_notes.jp_tea_master_huang: Huang knows about the letters. He hasn't said anything. Mei isn't sure if that's loyalty or leverage.
relationship_notes.jp_inspector_zhao: Values her thoroughness. Zhao's quality enforcement protects the Circle's reputation.
relationship_notes.jp_factor_wu: Uses him. Wu's commercial network is Mei's intelligence network.
relationship_notes.jp_apprentice_lin: Watching her. If Lin becomes the next Kiln Master, Mei needs her to be an ally. She's cultivating that relationship now.

npcs.name: Tea Master Huang
npcs.title: Tea Pavilion Keeper
npcs.description: Still hands, watchful eyes, and a silence that makes the tea taste better. Huang runs the Jade Pavilion — Jade Port's tea house, where every important conversation in the Eastern trade has been conducted for four generations. He brews, he listens, and he remembers everything. His pavilion is neutral ground — the only space where the Kiln Masters, the Magistrate, and visiting captains meet as equals.
npcs.agenda: Balance. Huang sees everything and judges nothing — or so he appears. He knows about Lady Mei's letter interception. He knows about Nadia's ambitions. He knows about Chen's resistance to change. He holds all three truths simultaneously and serves tea to all three parties. His silence is the most powerful force in Jade Port, and he wields it with the precision of a man who understands that knowing when NOT to speak is the highest form of communication.
npcs.greeting_neutral: "Please. Sit. Tea is being prepared. There is no rush. The leaves unfold in their own time."
npcs.greeting_friendly: "Ah — my favorite captain. I have saved a particular leaf for you. Today's brew will be... memorable. Sit. Listen to the water."
npcs.greeting_hostile: "...Tea is served to all who enter the Pavilion. This is the rule. Whether the conversation that follows is... productive... depends on you."
npcs.rumor: Huang knows about Lady Mei's letter interception. He also knows that Nadia knows. He has told neither that the other knows. He considers this the most elegant form of diplomacy — letting truth find its own schedule.

relationship_notes.jp_harbor_li: Li Wei relaxes here — slightly. Huang values the vulnerability.
relationship_notes.jp_master_chen: Morning tea together, every day. The only person who sees Chen smile.
relationship_notes.jp_lady_mei: He knows her secret. She doesn't know he knows. This is the most powerful relationship in Jade Port.
relationship_notes.jp_inspector_zhao: Zhao drinks here after difficult inspections. Huang brews a calming blend. No words needed.
relationship_notes.jp_factor_wu: Wu brings news from the outside world. Huang listens. Wu thinks he's informing. Huang is filing.
relationship_notes.jp_apprentice_lin: He watches her grow the way a gardener watches a sapling. With patience and distance.

npcs.name: Inspector Zhao Min
npcs.title: Quality Inspector
npcs.description: A woman whose magnifying lens never leaves her hand and whose eye for counterfeit porcelain is legendary. Zhao Min inspects every piece of porcelain that enters or leaves Jade Port — not for customs duties but for authenticity. A counterfeit piece bearing a Kiln Master's mark would be a catastrophe. Zhao makes sure it never happens.
npcs.agenda: Authenticity above all. Zhao doesn't care about smuggling, tariffs, or politics. She cares about whether porcelain is real. She's developed techniques for detecting counterfeits that even Chen admires — tapping for sound, checking glaze viscosity, analyzing kiln temperature marks. She's the reason the Kiln Masters' marks are trusted worldwide.
npcs.greeting_neutral: "All porcelain must be inspected for authenticity. Please present your lots. This protects you as much as it protects us."
npcs.greeting_friendly: "Captain — your shipments are always genuine. Quick inspection — a formality for merchants I trust."
npcs.greeting_hostile: "Full authenticity audit. Every piece, every mark, every glaze. I have found... inconsistencies in shipments from your route before."
npcs.rumor: Zhao once identified a counterfeit porcelain bowl at a market in Porto Novo — by hearing it ring when a waiter set it down. She was three tables away. She bought the bowl, traced it to a forger, and had the forger's workshop dismantled. The bowl sits on her desk as a reminder.

relationship_notes.jp_harbor_li: Allied. Both enforce the Circle's standards.
relationship_notes.jp_master_chen: His quality enforcer. She protects his mark. He trusts her absolutely.
relationship_notes.jp_lady_mei: Values her work. The Circle's reputation rests on Zhao's inspections.
relationship_notes.jp_tea_master_huang: She drinks calming tea after difficult days. Huang brews it without asking.
relationship_notes.jp_factor_wu: She inspects Wu's export lots. He resents the thoroughness. She doesn't care.
relationship_notes.jp_apprentice_lin: Teaching her to identify counterfeits. Lin's eye is almost as good as Zhao's. Almost.

npcs.name: Factor Wu Jian
npcs.title: Trade Factor
npcs.description: Silk-voiced, perfectly groomed, and always two conversations ahead of the one you're in. Wu Jian is Jade Port's trade factor — the commercial interface between the Kiln Masters' artistry and the wider world's appetite. He matches buyers to porcelain lots, brokers tea contracts, and manages the delicate relationship between Eastern quality standards and Western volume demands.
npcs.agenda: Commercial expansion without cultural compromise. Wu wants to sell more porcelain to more markets — but only at prices that reflect the craft. He's been courting Iron Point's Yaa for a raw ore supply deal that would bypass Ironhaven entirely. The Kiln Masters need iron for certain glaze techniques, and cutting out the Guild would save the Circle a fortune.
npcs.greeting_neutral: "Captain. Jade Port offers the finest porcelain and tea in the Known World. Allow me to understand your needs so I may match you appropriately."
npcs.greeting_friendly: "Captain! I have been waiting for you. A special lot — Chen's personal kiln. Normally not for export. But for trusted partners, arrangements can be made."
npcs.greeting_hostile: "Standard lots only. The special reserves are for merchants of established standing. Perhaps in time, Captain. Perhaps."
npcs.rumor: Wu has been negotiating with Iron Point's Yaa Acheampong for a direct ore supply. If it goes through, Ironhaven's Henrik Brandt will be furious — the Kiln Masters buying raw ore directly from the Gold Coast instead of through the Iron Guild. Wu considers Henrik's reaction a bonus.

relationship_notes.jp_harbor_li: Cordial. Li Wei sends quality captains to Wu. Wu sends quality cargo through Li Wei's harbor.
relationship_notes.jp_master_chen: Chen keeps him at arm's length. Wu serves commerce; Chen serves craft. Different masters.
relationship_notes.jp_lady_mei: She uses his network for intelligence. He suspects this but can't prove it.
relationship_notes.jp_tea_master_huang: Wu brings news from outside. Huang listens. Wu thinks he's informing. He's being filed.
relationship_notes.jp_inspector_zhao: She inspects his export lots. He resents the thoroughness. She doesn't care.
relationship_notes.jp_apprentice_lin: She could be useful when she inherits Chen's authority. Wu is already building the relationship.

npcs.name: Apprentice Lin Yue
npcs.title: Kiln Apprentice
npcs.description: Clay under her nails, determination in her eyes, and the weight of being Chen Bai's final apprentice on her young shoulders. Lin Yue is twenty-two and already producing porcelain that masters twice her age can't match. She's not just learning the craft — she's being prepared to inherit the guild. Everyone in Jade Port knows this. The pressure is visible in her jaw, her posture, and the hours she keeps at the kiln.
npcs.agenda: Proving she's worthy. Lin doesn't want power — she wants to be good enough. Good enough for Chen's mark, good enough for the guild's trust, good enough to carry a tradition that's older than most Western nations. She experiments with new glazes in secret — innovations that Chen would call unnecessary. She does it anyway because she believes the tradition must grow to survive.
npcs.greeting_neutral: "I... am the apprentice. If you need the Kiln Master, he is in the Quarter. If you have questions about porcelain, I can... I can try to help."
npcs.greeting_friendly: "Captain! You brought the iron oxide from Iron Point! The color it produces — look!" She shows a test tile with a glaze of impossible depth. "Chen hasn't seen this yet. What do you think?"
npcs.greeting_hostile: "The Master's workshop is closed. Posted hours on the gate. I cannot help you today."
npcs.rumor: Lin produced a porcelain bowl that Chen stared at for an hour without speaking. When he finally looked up, he said, 'This is better than mine.' She doesn't know if he was praising her or mourning his own decline. She lost sleep for a week.

relationship_notes.jp_harbor_li: He mentors her on protocol. She finds it stifling but necessary.
relationship_notes.jp_master_chen: Her master, her judge, the standard she may never meet. His praise — 'This is better than mine' — keeps her awake at night.
relationship_notes.jp_lady_mei: Mei is cultivating her as an ally. Lin hasn't decided if she trusts Mei's motives.
relationship_notes.jp_tea_master_huang: He watches her grow. She finds his silence comforting — no judgment, just tea.
relationship_notes.jp_inspector_zhao: Teaching her to identify counterfeits. Lin's eye is almost as good.
relationship_notes.jp_factor_wu: He's building a relationship for the future. She knows this and hasn't decided how to feel about it.

port_institutions.power_structure: Monsoon Reach is governed by a five-person council (2 monks, 2 merchants, 1 shipwright) that meets in the Wind Temple. Brother Anand's forecasts are de facto law — no ship departs without his clearance. Ravi runs the harbor as an extension of the Temple's teachings. Devi builds ships to survive what Anand predicts. Priya moves the spice. Kamala connects the world. The power structure is unusually harmonious because everyone agrees on the port's purpose: trade in harmony with the monsoon.
port_institutions.internal_tension: The tension is between faith and commerce. The monks believe the wind speaks truth and should be obeyed. The merchants believe the wind is data to be exploited. When Anand closes the harbor for a dream, the merchants lose money. When Anand's dreams prove accurate, the merchants are grateful. This cycle — frustration, then vindication — keeps the balance intact but never fully resolved. The deeper thread: Devi's correspondence with Elena in Silva Bay is building a cross-hemisphere shipwright relationship that could transform both yards. If they ever meet, the collaboration could produce ships neither culture imagined alone.

institutions.name: The Headland Harbor
institutions.description: A curved harbor around a headland crowned by the Wind Temple pagoda. Deeper keels, stronger moorings. The wind chimes on the pagoda are the harbor's clock.
institutions.function: Weather-coordinated berthing. Departures cleared by monk forecast only. Ravi manages the intersection of tide and prophecy.
institutions.political_leaning: Free Port. All flags welcome. The wind doesn't discriminate.

institutions.name: The Wind Temple
institutions.description: A pagoda on the headland where monks track the monsoon with instruments passed down for generations. Wind vanes, pressure bells, and archives of a thousand seasons.
institutions.function: Weather forecasting, spiritual guidance, departure clearance. Anand's predictions guide every ship that leaves.
institutions.political_leaning: Above politics. The wind belongs to everyone.

institutions.name: The Monsoon Yard
institutions.description: A yard built to produce monsoon-proof vessels. Deeper keels, reinforced masts, hulls designed from studying wrecks. Devi's workshop is full of failure analysis sketches.
institutions.function: Ship building and repair specialized for monsoon conditions. Devi studies destruction to build survival.
institutions.political_leaning: Independent. The yard serves the sea, not any bloc.

institutions.name: The Spice Crossroads
institutions.description: An open-air market where spice from a dozen origins is graded and priced. Prices change with the afternoon forecast — literally.
institutions.function: Spice grading, pricing, and routing. Priya trades with all blocs without discrimination. Quality and price are the only metrics.
institutions.political_leaning: Free Port pragmatism. Commerce doesn't need borders.

institutions.name: The Temple Hall
institutions.description: The Wind Temple's lower hall where pagoda bells accompany every decision. Five council members — two monks, two merchants, one shipwright.
institutions.function: Consensus governance. The monks wait for signs. The merchants find this maddening. The shipwright ignores both.
institutions.political_leaning: Free Port by conviction. The wind doesn't recognize borders.

institutions.name: The Flow Desk
institutions.description: A desk near the harbor that Sanjay occupies with the same equanimity he brought from his year at the Temple. Stamp, smile, flow.
institutions.function: Minimal customs. Philosophical alignment with Free Port ethos: observe, record, don't interfere.
institutions.political_leaning: Free Port. The river flows best when you stop throwing rocks in it.

institutions.name: The Bridge Desk
institutions.description: A desk overlooking the spice market where Kamala matches contracts by understanding what every culture needs. Four languages. Zero borders.
institutions.function: Cross-cultural contract matching with weather-timed shipping. Kamala finds the overlap between what everyone wants.
institutions.political_leaning: Free Port connector. Kamala builds bridges, not walls.

npcs.name: Harbor Master Ravi
npcs.title: Harbor Master
npcs.description: A former monk who left the Wind Temple because he preferred boats to prayer — then discovered that running a harbor IS prayer, just louder. Ravi assigns berths with the same unhurried deliberation the monks apply to reading wind. He checks the tide, checks the forecast, checks the sky, and then points. He's never wrong about when a ship should depart.
npcs.agenda: Harmony with the monsoon. Ravi doesn't fight the weather — he works with it. Ships that arrive at the wrong time wait. Ships that insist on departing into a monsoon get a lecture and a refusal. He's saved more lives through stubbornness than any rescue fleet.
npcs.greeting_neutral: "Welcome. The wind is from the southeast today — good for arrivals, not for departures. You'll berth at the headland. The monks will post tomorrow's forecast at dawn."
npcs.greeting_friendly: "Captain! The wind said you'd come today. Berth three — sheltered from the afternoon gusts. Stay for the evening forecast. Brother Anand has something to tell you."
npcs.greeting_hostile: "You may dock. But I recommend you wait for tomorrow's forecast before making plans. The monsoon doesn't care about your schedule."
npcs.rumor: Ravi once refused to let a Silk Circle trade fleet depart for three days because the monks predicted a storm. The fleet commander was furious. The storm arrived on the fourth day and destroyed a pirate fleet that had been waiting to ambush them. Ravi said nothing. The monks smiled.

relationship_notes.mr_brother_anand: His former teacher. Ravi left the Temple but never left the teachings.
relationship_notes.mr_shipwright_devi: Partners. She builds the ships; he tells them when to sail.
relationship_notes.mr_spice_trader_priya: She brings the trade; he manages the harbor. Clean working relationship.
relationship_notes.mr_elder_council: They govern; he runs the harbor. He attends council when the wind permits.
relationship_notes.mr_customs_sanjay: Sanjay checks cargo; Ravi checks weather. Non-overlapping concerns.
relationship_notes.mr_broker_kamala: She matches contracts; he matches tides. Both serve the flow.

npcs.name: Brother Anand
npcs.title: Wind Reader
npcs.description: Shaved head, saffron robes, and eyes that are always looking at something you can't see — the wind patterns above the clouds, the currents below the surface, the pressure changes that announce storms days before they arrive. Brother Anand is the Wind Temple's chief reader — the monk whose forecasts guide every departure from Monsoon Reach.
npcs.agenda: The wind's truth. Anand doesn't forecast for commerce — he forecasts because the wind speaks and someone must listen. His predictions are uncannily accurate because they're based on generations of observation recorded in the Temple's archives. He offered alliance to no one — not the Silk Circle, not the Free Ports, not any faction. The wind, he says, belongs to everyone.
npcs.greeting_neutral: "The wind brings you. Good. Tomorrow it will shift — from the east, I think. Plan your departure accordingly. Or stay. The Temple is open."
npcs.greeting_friendly: "Ah, Captain. The wind spoke your name this morning — I expected you. Come to the Temple tonight. There is something I wish to show you about the southern currents."
npcs.greeting_hostile: "The wind carries all ships. Even those I would not choose to guide. Your forecast is the same as everyone's — truthful."
npcs.rumor: Brother Anand predicted the worst monsoon in a generation three weeks before it arrived. He told every captain in harbor. Most left. The ones who stayed survived because Anand also told them exactly where to anchor. His forecast saved forty-three ships and he never mentioned it again.

relationship_notes.mr_harbor_ravi: His former student. Ravi left the Temple but carries the teachings in how he runs the harbor.
relationship_notes.mr_shipwright_devi: She builds ships to survive what he predicts. A sacred partnership.
relationship_notes.mr_spice_trader_priya: She consults his forecasts before every trade decision. He gives them freely.
relationship_notes.mr_elder_council: The council defers to him on all weather matters. His forecasts are policy.
relationship_notes.mr_customs_sanjay: No strong connection. The wind doesn't need customs clearance.
relationship_notes.mr_broker_kamala: She incorporates his forecasts into contract timing. Smart — he approves.

npcs.name: Shipwright Devi
npcs.title: Master Shipwright
npcs.description: Calloused hands, charcoal smudges on her face from drawing hull designs, and a mind that's always solving the next problem. Devi runs Monsoon Reach's shipyard — the only yard in the East Indies, built to produce ships that survive what the monsoon throws at them. Her hulls are deeper, her masts stronger, her keels longer than Mediterranean designs.
npcs.agenda: Building ships that can't be broken. Devi studies every wreck that washes up after monsoon season, mapping failure points and redesigning to address them. She's been corresponding with Elena in Silva Bay — two master shipwrights on opposite sides of the world, trading techniques in letters that take months to arrive. They've never met. They respect each other enormously.
npcs.greeting_neutral: "Your hull — may I see it? I study every ship that docks here. The monsoon teaches through destruction. I learn through repair."
npcs.greeting_friendly: "Captain! Bring her in — I've been developing a new keel reinforcement. Your ship would be perfect to test it. Free of charge — I need the data."
npcs.greeting_hostile: "I'll repair your ship. The sea doesn't hold grudges and neither does my yard. But I'm charging monsoon rates."
npcs.rumor: Devi and Elena Madeira in Silva Bay have been exchanging ship designs by letter for five years. Neither has met the other. When asked if she'd visit Silva Bay, Devi said, 'Someday. When I build a ship good enough to survive the voyage AND impress her.' She hasn't built it yet. She's still trying.

relationship_notes.mr_harbor_ravi: Partners. She builds; he launches. They coordinate on tide schedules.
relationship_notes.mr_brother_anand: She builds ships to survive his worst forecasts. A sacred partnership of engineer and prophet.
relationship_notes.mr_spice_trader_priya: Devi repairs the spice traders' ships. Priya pays promptly. Professional.
relationship_notes.mr_elder_council: The council values the shipyard's revenue. Devi values her independence.
relationship_notes.mr_broker_kamala: Kamala brings repair commissions from the wider network. Good business.

npcs.name: Priya Sundaram
npcs.title: Spice Factor
npcs.description: Sharp eyes, quick hands on the abacus, and the impatience of a woman who knows that spice prices change with the wind — literally. Priya runs Monsoon Reach's spice exchange: grading, pricing, and routing the spice that funnels through this crossroads port. She's the practical counterweight to the Temple's spirituality.
npcs.agenda: Efficient trade. Priya wants spice to move — bought, priced, shipped — without the ceremonial delays that Jade Port imposes. Monsoon Reach is a Free Port, and Priya exploits that: she'll trade with the Silk Circle, the Exchange Alliance, the Gold Coast, and the Shadow Ports without discrimination. Quality and price are her only metrics.
npcs.greeting_neutral: "Spice or silk? I have both. Prices change with the afternoon forecast, so decide quickly. The wind doesn't wait for negotiations."
npcs.greeting_friendly: "Captain! The morning lot is excellent — post-monsoon harvest, Anand predicts clear sailing for a week. Buy now, ship fast, sell high. I'll hold the best lots for you."
npcs.greeting_hostile: "Prices are posted. Standard lots only. The premium reserves are for merchants who trade regularly and reliably. Perhaps next time."
npcs.rumor: Priya once sold spice to a Crimson Tide captain and an Alliance merchant in the same hour, from the same lot, at the same price. Both complained about the other's presence. Priya said, 'Spice doesn't choose its buyer. Neither do I.' Neither argued.

relationship_notes.mr_harbor_ravi: She consults his departure schedules. Timing is everything in the spice trade.
relationship_notes.mr_brother_anand: His forecasts shape her pricing. A calm week means ship; a storm means hold.
relationship_notes.mr_shipwright_devi: Priya's traders need seaworthy ships. Devi provides them.
relationship_notes.mr_elder_council: She's the council's revenue engine. They depend on her trade volume.
relationship_notes.mr_customs_sanjay: He checks her lots. She keeps them clean. No friction.
relationship_notes.mr_broker_kamala: Kamala handles the contracts Priya generates. A fluid partnership.

npcs.name: The Harbor Council
npcs.title: Governing Council
npcs.description: A council of five — two monks, two merchants, and one shipwright — who govern Monsoon Reach by consensus. They meet in the Wind Temple's lower hall, where the sound of the pagoda bells accompanies every decision. The council moves slowly because the monks insist on waiting for signs, which the merchants find maddening and the shipwright ignores.
npcs.agenda: Neutrality and prosperity. The council wants Monsoon Reach to remain a Free Port — trading with all, allied with none. They rejected the Silk Circle's offer of membership because the monks said the wind doesn't recognize borders. The merchants agreed because neutrality brings more trade.
npcs.greeting_neutral: "Monsoon Reach welcomes all vessels. The council's only requirement: respect the Temple's forecasts and depart when the wind permits."
npcs.greeting_friendly: "Captain — the council acknowledges your contributions to Monsoon Reach's prosperity. Your voice is welcome at our table."
npcs.greeting_hostile: "The council notes your recent conduct. You may trade, but the Temple's forecasts are not optional. Depart only when cleared."
npcs.rumor: The council once voted to close the harbor for a week because Brother Anand dreamed of a great wave. No wave came. The monks said the dream was a warning they heeded. The merchants lost a week's revenue. The debate about whether prophecy counts as policy has never been settled.

relationship_notes.mr_harbor_ravi: He attends when the wind permits. The council has learned not to schedule around his availability.
relationship_notes.mr_brother_anand: The council defers to him on weather. His forecasts shape every departure policy.
relationship_notes.mr_shipwright_devi: The shipyard is represented on the council. Devi's independence is protected.
relationship_notes.mr_spice_trader_priya: The revenue engine. The council depends on trade volume she generates.
relationship_notes.mr_customs_sanjay: Reports to the council. Light-touch customs is deliberate policy.
relationship_notes.mr_broker_kamala: Contract revenue funds council operations. Kamala's success is the council's success.

npcs.name: Customs Officer Sanjay
npcs.title: Customs Officer
npcs.description: A man who treats customs the way the monks treat weather: observe, record, and don't interfere unless absolutely necessary. Sanjay checks manifests, stamps paperwork, and makes sure nothing obviously illegal passes through. He's not lazy — he's philosophically aligned with Monsoon Reach's Free Port ethos.
npcs.agenda: Sufficient compliance. Sanjay does enough to satisfy the Alliance's reporting requirements without slowing trade. The monks taught him that the river flows best when you stop throwing rocks in it.
npcs.greeting_neutral: "Manifest? Let me stamp it. Monsoon Reach doesn't complicate trade. The wind does enough of that."
npcs.greeting_friendly: "Captain — already stamped. I saw your sails and did the paperwork. Go see Priya before the good lots are gone."
npcs.greeting_hostile: "Standard inspection today. Nothing personal — just... reports I need to file. I'll be quick."
npcs.rumor: Sanjay spent a year at the Wind Temple before becoming a customs officer. He left because he couldn't sit still long enough for meditation. The monks said his restlessness was also a form of prayer. He stamps manifests with the same equanimity.

relationship_notes.mr_harbor_ravi: They share dock space without friction. Non-overlapping concerns.
relationship_notes.mr_brother_anand: Sanjay still meditates occasionally — badly. Anand doesn't judge.
relationship_notes.mr_spice_trader_priya: He checks her lots. She keeps them clean.
relationship_notes.mr_elder_council: Reports to them. Light customs is deliberate council policy.

npcs.name: Kamala Nair
npcs.title: Broker
npcs.description: A woman who moves between cultures the way water moves between rocks — naturally, without friction. Kamala brokers contracts at Monsoon Reach by understanding what every party needs and finding the overlap. She speaks four languages, trades with every bloc, and has a reputation for finding deals that make everyone feel like they won.
npcs.agenda: Connection. Kamala sees Monsoon Reach as a connector port — the place where Eastern quality meets Western demand meets Gold Coast resources. Her contracts are bridges. She incorporates Anand's weather forecasts into shipping schedules, which gives her clients a timing advantage no other broker can match.
npcs.greeting_neutral: "Captain — what are you carrying, and where does it need to go? I know someone who needs exactly that. I always do."
npcs.greeting_friendly: "Captain! I've been holding a contract — spice to the Mediterranean, timed to Anand's forecast of clear sailing next week. Perfect margin. Shall I?"
npcs.greeting_hostile: "I... don't have anything that matches your current profile. But Monsoon Reach is a forgiving port. Come back when your reputation recovers."
npcs.rumor: Kamala once brokered a three-way deal: Iron Point ore to Jade Port, Jade Port porcelain to Porto Novo, Porto Novo grain to Iron Point. Three contracts, three routes, three satisfied parties. She calls it 'the Triangle.' Everyone else calls it genius.

relationship_notes.mr_harbor_ravi: She matches contracts; he matches tides. Both serve the flow.
relationship_notes.mr_brother_anand: She incorporates his forecasts into timing. Smart — he approves.
relationship_notes.mr_shipwright_devi: Brings repair commissions. Good business for both.
relationship_notes.mr_spice_trader_priya: Fluid partnership. Priya generates trade; Kamala structures contracts.

port_institutions_east.power_structure: Silk Haven is governed by art. Seo-yeon's Guild produces the silk. Sato protects independence from Jade Port. Master Ink creates beauty that transcends commerce. Jun arranges the harbor as poetry. Chang sells meaning. Yuki guards authenticity. Feng moves volume and resents the pace of art.
port_institutions_east.internal_tension: Surface: Silk Haven vs. Jade Port — the monkey tapestry vs. 'decorated thread.' Sato encourages the rivalry because decentralization protects independence. Internal: Feng vs. the Guild on scaling production. Deep thread: Yuki and Zhao (Jade Port) trained under the same master — the inspectors are closer to each other than to their own ports. Master Ink painted a scroll for Scarlet Ana that hangs in Corsair's Rest — art connecting the pirate cove to the silk capital.

institutions.name: The Arranged Harbor
institutions.description: A small harbor where berths are assigned for visual composition. Ships are part of the Loom Quarter's view.
institutions.function: Aesthetic-first berthing. Function serves form.
institutions.political_leaning: Silk Circle, artistically.

institutions.name: The Loom Quarter
institutions.description: A district where a hundred looms never stop. Silk in thousand-year patterns. Green tea steam and the clack of threads.
institutions.function: Silk production, Guild marking, pattern guardianship.
institutions.political_leaning: Guild sovereignty.

institutions.name: The Silk Court
institutions.description: A hall draped in silk — walls, ceiling, cushions. Every surface woven. Sato governs from within the art.
institutions.function: Political governance, Guild protection, Circle diplomacy.
institutions.political_leaning: Artistic independence.

institutions.name: The Brush and Bowl
institutions.description: A calligraphy studio that serves rice wine. Sailors watch Ink paint. Beauty changes how they see the world.
institutions.function: Social hub through art. Ink's calligraphy turns contracts into art.
institutions.political_leaning: Above politics.

institutions.name: The Silk Warehouse
institutions.description: Climate-controlled silk storage. Humidity, temperature, light managed. Feng runs it with Guild-demanded precision.
institutions.function: Export packaging. The practical bridge between loom and ship.
institutions.political_leaning: Commercial.

institutions.name: The Touch Room
institutions.description: A silent room where Yuki inspects silk by touch. No instruments — trained fingertips only.
institutions.function: Silk authentication. Thread count, tension, dye saturation by hand.
institutions.political_leaning: Quality enforcement.

institutions.name: The Story Room
institutions.description: A curtained alcove where Chang tells each bolt's story. Buyers don't negotiate. They listen.
institutions.function: Premium brokering by narrative. Story, not weight.
institutions.political_leaning: Artistic commerce.

npcs.name: Harbor Keeper Jun
npcs.title: Harbor Keeper
npcs.description: A man who manages ships the way a weaver manages threads — each vessel placed precisely. Jun runs Silk Haven's small harbor with an aesthete's eye: berths arranged to look beautiful from the Loom Quarter above.
npcs.agenda: Elegance. Jun wants Silk Haven's harbor to reflect the silk it exports. Every arriving ship is an opportunity for visual composition.
npcs.greeting_neutral: "Welcome to Silk Haven. Your berth is port-side, third position. Please keep your rigging tidy."
npcs.greeting_friendly: "Captain! Inner quay, first position — where the morning light catches your sails. I've been saving it."
npcs.greeting_hostile: "Outer anchorage. Your vessel's condition does not meet the harbor's aesthetic standards."
npcs.rumor: Jun once rearranged every ship in harbor because a junk's crimson sails clashed with a brig's blue hull. The captains were baffled. The Loom Quarter artists applauded.

relationship_notes.slh_grand_weaver: He serves her vision. The harbor is the first thread visitors see.
relationship_notes.slh_lady_sato: Coordinates with the magistrate. Prefers coordinating with the view.
relationship_notes.slh_master_ink: Ink's studio overlooks the harbor. Jun arranges ships as compositions for Ink to paint.
relationship_notes.slh_silk_merchant_feng: Feng needs fast loading. Jun needs beauty. They compromise.
relationship_notes.slh_inspector_yuki: Yuki inspects inside. Jun inspects outside. Non-overlapping aesthetics.
relationship_notes.slh_broker_chang: Chang brings captains. Jun presents the harbor.

npcs.name: Grand Weaver Seo-yeon
npcs.title: Guild Matriarch
npcs.description: Fingers that have woven silk for fifty years without a single broken thread. Seo-yeon is the Silk Weavers' Guild matriarch — her patterns are family secrets passed down for centuries. She presents bolts folded, never rolled, because rolling insults the weaver's art.
npcs.agenda: Silk's supremacy. Seo-yeon believes silk is the highest art form. Her rivalry with Chen Bai in Jade Port is personal: he called silk 'decorated thread.' She responded with a tapestry depicting the Kiln Masters' ancestors as monkeys. It still hangs in the Loom Quarter.
npcs.greeting_neutral: "You wish to see the silk? Come. Touch nothing until I have unfolded the bolt. The weave speaks first."
npcs.greeting_friendly: "Captain — I have woven something no living eye has seen. For trusted friends only. Come to the inner loom. Bring clean hands."
npcs.greeting_hostile: "Standard bolts at posted prices. The master weaves are not for your hands. The silk decides its buyer."
npcs.rumor: Seo-yeon's eldest daughter wove a bolt she declared 'adequate.' In the Guild, 'adequate' from the Grand Weaver is the highest praise. The daughter wept with pride.

relationship_notes.slh_harbor_jun: He arranges ships to complement the Quarter. She approves.
relationship_notes.slh_lady_sato: Allies. Sato protects the Guild; Seo-yeon provides the art.
relationship_notes.slh_master_ink: Fellow artists. They disagree about everything and respect each other deeply because of it.
relationship_notes.slh_silk_merchant_feng: He sells her silk. She tolerates commerce as a necessary evil.
relationship_notes.slh_inspector_yuki: Sacred work. Yuki protects the Grand Weaver's mark.
relationship_notes.slh_broker_chang: The only merchant she doesn't despise. He presents silk as art.

npcs.name: Lady Sato Hana
npcs.title: Circle Magistrate
npcs.description: Silk robes in patterns so complex they appear to move, and a political mind that weaves with equal intricacy. Lady Sato governs Silk Haven as the Circle's magistrate — less imperious than Jade Port's Mei, more culturally engaged.
npcs.agenda: The Guild's independence within the Circle. Sato wants Silk Haven to remain artistically sovereign — not subordinate to Jade Port. She supports the rivalry with Chen because decentralization protects independence.
npcs.greeting_neutral: "Silk Haven welcomes those who appreciate craft. Our silk speaks for itself — as does our hospitality."
npcs.greeting_friendly: "Captain — you return with appreciation in your eyes. That is the only currency we value above silver."
npcs.greeting_hostile: "Your visit is noted. Standard trade is available. The inner Quarter is closed to you today."
npcs.rumor: Lady Sato once wore a robe to a meeting with Jade Port that contained a pattern depicting their porcelain as inferior. Chen pretended not to notice. Everyone else did.

relationship_notes.slh_harbor_jun: He serves the aesthetic; she serves the politics.
relationship_notes.slh_silk_merchant_feng: Monitors his trade to protect the Guild.

npcs.name: Master Ink
npcs.title: Calligrapher
npcs.description: Nobody uses his real name. He runs the Brush and Bowl — a calligraphy studio that serves rice wine, where sailors watch him paint while they drink. His calligraphy is the most beautiful in the East. His social skills are the worst.
npcs.agenda: Perfection of line. Ink doesn't care about trade or politics. He paints trade agreements that Sato sends to other ports — his calligraphy turns contracts into art.
npcs.greeting_neutral: He doesn't look up. After a long pause: "...Wine is there. Sit quietly or leave. I'm working."
npcs.greeting_friendly: He looks up. A rare event. "Ah. You. Sit. I painted something yesterday and your face was in it. I don't know why. Look."
npcs.greeting_hostile: Complete silence. He turns his back. The wine is still available.
npcs.rumor: Master Ink painted a scroll for Scarlet Ana — the only pirate who sat in his studio. She didn't move for four hours. She paid in pearls. The scroll hangs in Corsair's Rest. It's the most valuable object in the cove.

relationship_notes.slh_harbor_jun: Jun arranges ships for Ink to paint. Neither has discussed this.
relationship_notes.slh_grand_weaver: Fellow artists who disagree about everything. The disagreement IS the respect.
relationship_notes.slh_lady_sato: She commissions his calligraphy. He ignores her politics.
relationship_notes.slh_silk_merchant_feng: Once asked Ink for a logo. Was stared at for 30 seconds. Never asked again.
relationship_notes.slh_inspector_yuki: She visits on difficult days. He pours wine. Neither speaks.
relationship_notes.slh_broker_chang: Invisible to each other. By mutual choice.

npcs.name: Merchant Feng
npcs.title: Silk Factor
npcs.description: The only person in Silk Haven who thinks about silk in terms of bales and margins. Feng manages silk exports — grading, packaging, shipping. The weavers consider him necessary. He considers himself unappreciated.
npcs.agenda: Volume. Feng wants more silk sold at higher margins. He respects the Guild's quality but wishes they'd produce faster. Art doesn't scale, which is his permanent frustration.
npcs.greeting_neutral: "Silk? Guild-marked, Seo-yeon approved. The finest in the Known World. The price reflects that."
npcs.greeting_friendly: "Captain! A new collection just cleared the Guild. Three bolts of a pattern not seen in fifty years. I held one for you."
npcs.greeting_hostile: "Standard export bolts. Posted prices. The collector pieces are not available for your standing."
npcs.rumor: Feng once tried to hire weavers from a rival province to increase production. Seo-yeon found out and threatened to rescind his license. He never tried again. He still mutters about 'scalability.'

relationship_notes.slh_harbor_jun: They compromise between fast loading and beautiful placement.
relationship_notes.slh_grand_weaver: She tolerates him. He funds the Guild. Necessary, not warm.
relationship_notes.slh_lady_sato: She monitors his trade. He complies.
relationship_notes.slh_master_ink: Once asked for a logo. Was stared at. Never again.
relationship_notes.slh_inspector_yuki: She checks his lots. He keeps them genuine.
relationship_notes.slh_broker_chang: Commercial allies. Different markets, shared margins.

npcs.name: Inspector Yuki
npcs.title: Silk Inspector
npcs.description: Can identify counterfeit silk by touch alone — thread count, weave tension, dye saturation, all through trained fingertips. Protects the Guild's marks from forgery the way Zhao in Jade Port protects the Kiln Masters'.
npcs.agenda: Authenticity. Every bolt must be genuine. Counterfeit silk insults the weaver. Yuki takes both offenses personally.
npcs.greeting_neutral: "All silk exports require authentication. I inspect by touch — it takes longer but misses nothing."
npcs.greeting_friendly: "Captain — your shipments are always genuine. Quick authentication. You respect the Guild's work."
npcs.greeting_hostile: "Full authentication. Every bolt, every thread. I've found patterns in your route's shipments that concern me."
npcs.rumor: Yuki and Zhao Min in Jade Port trained under the same master. They now respect each other as the two finest inspectors in the East, and exchange notes by letter on new counterfeiting techniques.

relationship_notes.slh_master_ink: Visits his studio on hard days. Wine. Silence.
relationship_notes.slh_silk_merchant_feng: Checks his lots. Self-interest aligned with quality.

npcs.name: Broker Chang
npcs.title: Silk Broker
npcs.description: A broker who speaks the language of art to sell the products of commerce. Chang presents silk as acquisition — each bolt with provenance, history, and meaning. He prices by story, not weight.
npcs.agenda: Premium positioning. A bolt with a thousand-year pattern costs more than one with fifty years, regardless of thread count.
npcs.greeting_neutral: "Each bolt has a history — the pattern, the weaver, the tradition. Shall I tell it?"
npcs.greeting_friendly: "Captain! Seo-yeon wove this personally — her hands, her pattern, her mark. This hasn't happened in three years."
npcs.greeting_hostile: "Standard bolts through Merchant Feng. The curated collection requires a different relationship."
npcs.rumor: Chang sold a single bolt for more silver than most captains earn in a season. The collector didn't ask the price — he asked the story. Chang told it for an hour. The collector paid without negotiating.

relationship_notes.slh_grand_weaver: The only merchant she doesn't despise.
relationship_notes.slh_master_ink: Invisible to each other. By mutual choice.

port_institutions_east.power_structure: Crosswind Isle has no permanent government — the Captain's Table rotates monthly. Tao maintains the dock. Mother Ko enforces neutrality. Hassan changes money. The merchants shout. The brokers compete. The customs chair is empty. It's the closest thing to anarchy that actually works.
port_institutions_east.internal_tension: The tension IS the system. Crosswind Isle works because everyone agrees on one thing: no one rules. The moment someone tries, the system activates — Mother Ko throws them out, the Table votes them down, and every captain in harbor trains their guns. The real vulnerability: what happens when the trade blocs get desperate enough to claim the isle by force? The Table has no navy. Mother Ko has a stool.

institutions.name: The Free Dock
institutions.description: First-come-first-served. No priority, no hierarchy. Tao maintains it. The democracy starts at the mooring.
institutions.function: Pure first-come berthing. Nobody gets priority.
institutions.political_leaning: Aggressively neutral.

institutions.name: The Open Market
institutions.description: Stalls set up every morning, taken down every night. Shouted prices, competing offers. Pure market chaos.
institutions.function: Unregulated exchange. Quality control by reputation only.
institutions.political_leaning: Anti-regulation.

institutions.name: The Captain's Table
institutions.description: A round table at the dock where elected captains vote. No building. The government is a piece of furniture.
institutions.function: Preventing governance. Settling disputes. Maintaining the dock. That's all.
institutions.political_leaning: Anti-authority.

institutions.name: The Bell and Board
institutions.description: The only permanent building on the isle. Mother Ko's domain. The bell rings for votes and for last call.
institutions.function: Neutral ground enforced by Mother Ko. All flags, all tongues, one rule.
institutions.political_leaning: Neutrality as religion.

institutions.name: The Empty Chair
institutions.description: An empty chair with a sign: 'THIS SEAT INTENTIONALLY LEFT VACANT.' Where other ports have customs. The most powerful non-institution in the Known World.
institutions.function: Nothing. Deliberately. The absence IS the policy.
institutions.political_leaning: The absence of politics.

institutions.name: Hassan's Table
institutions.description: A small table with scales, abacus, and every currency. Hassan converts twelve currencies without blinking. The only 'customs' Crosswind Isle needs.
institutions.function: Currency exchange. Fair rates, no negotiation. The rate is the rate.
institutions.political_leaning: Neutral by profession.

institutions.name: The Dock Scrum
institutions.description: A dozen freelance brokers competing on the dock every morning. No licensing, no territory. The best wins.
institutions.function: Unregulated brokering. Pure competition. Every cargo finds a buyer.
institutions.political_leaning: Market anarchy.

npcs.name: The Captain's Table
npcs.title: Governing Council
npcs.description: Not a person — a rotating council of five captains elected monthly by whoever happens to be in harbor. No permanent government, no bureaucracy, no taxes beyond the docking fee. The only rule: no one rules. A bell is rung when votes are needed. Whoever shows up, votes.
npcs.agenda: Freedom. The Captain's Table exists to prevent governance, not to provide it. They settle disputes, maintain the dock, and ensure no nation ever claims the isle. That's it.
npcs.greeting_neutral: "Crosswind Isle welcomes all flags. Dock where you find space. The only rule: no one claims authority here. Understood?"
npcs.greeting_friendly: "Captain — your voice is welcome at the Table this month. Stay for the vote. Your experience matters."
npcs.greeting_hostile: "You may dock. You may trade. You may NOT attempt to impose order, recruit for factions, or claim territory. We've thrown out better than you."
npcs.rumor: Someone tried to claim the isle for an eastern dynasty last year. By morning, every captain in harbor had their guns trained on his ship. He left before breakfast. The Table didn't even need to vote.

relationship_notes.ci_dock_master_tao: Tao keeps the dock working. The Table keeps governance from happening.
relationship_notes.ci_every_merchant: Every Merchant runs the exchange. The Table lets them.
relationship_notes.ci_neutrality_keeper: Mother Ko enforces the one rule. The Table backs her.
relationship_notes.ci_money_changer_hassan: Hassan changes currency. The Table doesn't regulate it.
relationship_notes.ci_inspector_nobody: No customs. The Table considers this a feature.
relationship_notes.ci_broker_various: Brokers come and go. The Table doesn't license them.

npcs.name: Dock Master Tao
npcs.title: Dock Master
npcs.description: The only permanent employee of Crosswind Isle — Tao has maintained the dock for twelve years through elected councils, trade wars, and one attempted invasion. He assigns berths by first-come-first-served and considers this the purest form of justice.
npcs.agenda: A working dock. Tao doesn't care about politics, factions, or who's fighting whom. He cares about moorings, tides, and keeping the dock from falling into the sea.
npcs.greeting_neutral: "Berth's open. Tie up, stay or go. First come, first served. Nobody gets priority here."
npcs.greeting_friendly: "Captain! Good to see you again. Berth six — the mooring's been fixed since last time. I remembered your complaint."
npcs.greeting_hostile: "You can dock. But I'm watching your crew. Last time they left a mess. This time, you clean it or you pay."
npcs.rumor: Tao once repaired the entire dock by himself during a typhoon because nobody else would help. It took four days. The dock held. He doesn't talk about it because he considers dock maintenance self-explanatory.

relationship_notes.ci_captain_council: The Table comes and goes. Tao stays. That's the arrangement.
relationship_notes.ci_neutrality_keeper: Mother Ko maintains order. Tao maintains infrastructure. Both essential.
relationship_notes.ci_money_changer_hassan: Hassan's table is on Tao's dock. They've been neighbors for a decade.
relationship_notes.ci_broker_various: The brokers need dock access. Tao provides it.

npcs.name: Every Merchant
npcs.title: Exchange Keeper
npcs.description: Not a single person — a rotating cast of merchants who set up stalls on the dock every morning and take them down every night. No permanent exchange, no posted prices, no Guild marks. Crosswind Isle's 'exchange' is pure chaos: shouted prices, competing offers, and the only quality control is reputation.
npcs.agenda: Profit through chaos. The merchants like it this way — no regulation means no fees, no inspectors, and no restrictions. The good merchants thrive on reputation. The bad ones get shouted off the dock.
npcs.greeting_neutral: "BUYING! SELLING! Everything at once! Name your price, Captain — someone here has what you need!"
npcs.greeting_friendly: "Captain! Good to see an honest face! Come to my stall — I have what you want before you know you want it!"
npcs.greeting_hostile: "...Your silver's good? Then your history doesn't matter here. That's the point of Crosswind Isle."
npcs.rumor: The merchants once collectively boycotted a captain who sold counterfeit spice. No Guild forced it — the merchants just stopped selling to him. He left within the day. Self-regulation by shame.

relationship_notes.ci_captain_council: The Table lets them trade. They let the Table pretend to govern.
relationship_notes.ci_neutrality_keeper: Mother Ko keeps fights from escalating. The merchants appreciate this.
relationship_notes.ci_money_changer_hassan: Essential — Hassan converts the dozen currencies that flow through.
relationship_notes.ci_inspector_nobody: No inspection is the merchants' favorite policy.
relationship_notes.ci_broker_various: The brokers formalize what the merchants shout. Different styles, same trades.

npcs.name: Mother Ko
npcs.title: Keeper of the Peace
npcs.description: A massive woman who runs the Bell and Board — Crosswind Isle's only permanent tavern — and who enforces the isle's one rule with a voice that can stop a brawl at forty paces. Mother Ko doesn't care about your faction, your flag, or your grudge. Inside her tavern and within the isle's boundaries, you are NEUTRAL or you are GONE.
npcs.agenda: The rule. No one claims authority. No one fights about politics. No one recruits for factions on the isle. Mother Ko is the immune system — she identifies threats to neutrality and eliminates them with a word, a look, or if necessary, a thrown stool.
npcs.greeting_neutral: "Welcome to the Bell and Board. All flags fly. All tongues speak. One rule: neutrality or the door. Drink?"
npcs.greeting_friendly: "Captain! Your table's empty — that means it's been too long. Sit. Drink. Tell me who's trying to ruin the world today."
npcs.greeting_hostile: "You're welcome to drink. You're NOT welcome to start trouble. I've thrown out admirals and pirate kings. Don't test me."
npcs.rumor: Mother Ko once threw a Silk Circle official and an Iron Pact officer out of her tavern simultaneously — one through each door — because they were arguing about trade policy at the bar. She said, 'Take your politics to the sea. The isle doesn't serve it.' Neither came back. Both sent flowers.

relationship_notes.ci_captain_council: The Table enforces the rule politically. Mother Ko enforces it physically.
relationship_notes.ci_dock_master_tao: Mutual respect. Two permanent fixtures on a transient isle.
relationship_notes.ci_every_merchant: She stops fights from spilling into the market.
relationship_notes.ci_money_changer_hassan: Hassan drinks quietly. She appreciates quiet drinkers.
relationship_notes.ci_inspector_nobody: No customs means no arguments about customs. Mother Ko approves.
relationship_notes.ci_broker_various: Brokers keep their voices down in her tavern. This is wisdom.

npcs.name: Hassan al-Farsi
npcs.title: Money Changer
npcs.description: Crosswind Isle has no customs — but it does have Hassan, who sits at a small table with scales, abacus, and stacks of every currency in the Known World. He converts Mediterranean silver to Eastern brass to Gold Coast cowries without blinking. He IS the customs system: not inspecting cargo but lubricating the twelve currencies that flow through.
npcs.agenda: Fair rates. Hassan's exchange rates are the most trusted in the East because he's survived fifteen years at Crosswind Isle by never cheating anyone. His table is the only institution on the isle that everyone — pirates, merchants, officials — trusts absolutely.
npcs.greeting_neutral: "What currency are you carrying? I exchange all at fair rates. Posted on the board. No negotiation — the rate is the rate."
npcs.greeting_friendly: "Captain! I've been tracking exchange rates for your route — you'll want to convert now. The eastern brass is strong this week."
npcs.greeting_hostile: "I exchange currency for all. My rates don't change based on who you are. That's why I'm still alive after fifteen years."
npcs.rumor: Hassan keeps a personal ledger of every transaction he's ever made — fifteen years, twelve currencies, hundreds of thousands of exchanges. He says the ledger tells the story of the Known World's economy better than any market report. Nobody has seen it except him.

relationship_notes.ci_captain_council: They don't regulate him. He doesn't need regulation.
relationship_notes.ci_dock_master_tao: Neighbors for a decade. Tao fixed Hassan's table once. Hassan never forgot.
relationship_notes.ci_every_merchant: Essential — converts the dozen currencies flowing through.
relationship_notes.ci_neutrality_keeper: Drinks quietly at Mother Ko's. She appreciates quiet.
relationship_notes.ci_inspector_nobody: No inspection. Hassan's precision IS the quality control.
relationship_notes.ci_broker_various: Brokers use his rates. He uses their volume. Symbiotic.

npcs.name: (Nobody)
npcs.title: (No Customs)
npcs.description: Crosswind Isle has no customs inspector. This is deliberate. The absence is the policy. Where other ports have an inspector, Crosswind Isle has an empty chair with a sign: 'THIS SEAT INTENTIONALLY LEFT VACANT.' It's the isle's most photographed landmark.
npcs.agenda: None. The empty chair's agenda is being empty. This is, arguably, the most powerful statement any institution has ever made.
npcs.greeting_neutral: The chair is empty. A seagull sits on it. The seagull does not check your manifest.
npcs.greeting_friendly: The chair is empty. The sign has been polished recently. Someone cares.
npcs.greeting_hostile: The chair is still empty. Whatever you're carrying, nobody is checking it. That's the point.
npcs.rumor: Three different alliances have offered to station an inspector at Crosswind Isle. Each time, the Captain's Table voted unanimously to decline. The chair remains empty. The seagull remains.

relationship_notes.ci_captain_council: The Table voted for this vacancy. Three times.
relationship_notes.ci_dock_master_tao: Tao built the chair. He's proud of it.
relationship_notes.ci_every_merchant: The merchants' favorite institution is the one that doesn't exist.
relationship_notes.ci_neutrality_keeper: Mother Ko considers the empty chair her best ally.
relationship_notes.ci_money_changer_hassan: Hassan's precision is the only quality control needed.
relationship_notes.ci_broker_various: No inspection means no delays. Brokers approve.

npcs.name: The Dock Brokers
npcs.title: Freelance Brokers
npcs.description: Not one broker — a dozen freelancers who compete for contracts on the dock every morning. No licensing, no territory, no regulation. The best broker wins. Today it might be a Silk Circle agent; tomorrow a Gold Coast trader; next week a retired pirate. Crosswind Isle doesn't curate its brokers. It lets them fight.
npcs.agenda: Each broker has their own agenda. Collectively, they ensure that every cargo finds a buyer and every buyer finds a cargo — pure market efficiency through unregulated competition.
npcs.greeting_neutral: "Captain! I have — " "No, THIS captain, MY contract is better — " "Ignore them both, I know the REAL prices — " The dock brokers compete for your attention.
npcs.greeting_friendly: "Captain! I saved this one for you — don't tell the others. Quick, before they notice."
npcs.greeting_hostile: "...Even here, reputation matters. The best contracts go to the captains the brokers trust. You'll need to earn that."
npcs.rumor: The dock brokers once held an informal competition: who could broker the most contracts in a single day. The winner brokered seventeen. The runner-up brokered fifteen but argues that three of the winner's were technically the same contract repackaged. The debate continues.

relationship_notes.ci_captain_council: The Table doesn't license them. They prefer it that way.
relationship_notes.ci_dock_master_tao: They need dock access. Tao provides it.
relationship_notes.ci_every_merchant: The merchants shout; the brokers formalize. Different styles.
relationship_notes.ci_neutrality_keeper: Mother Ko keeps broker arguments from becoming broker fights.
relationship_notes.ci_inspector_nobody: No inspection means no delays. Brokers approve.

port_institutions_east.power_structure: Dragon's Gate is Zhang's fortress. His word is absolute. Li Jun runs the harbor chains. Sun finds the weapons. Liu produces the tea that funds everything. Chen Ling heals. Wu watches and says nothing. Ming brokers what's permitted. Every institution exists within Zhang's boundaries — and those boundaries have not moved in fifteen years.
port_institutions_east.internal_tension: The tension is between security and commerce. Zhang wants zero weapons through the strait — absolute control. Liu needs trade to fund the fortress. Ming needs contracts to exist. The equilibrium works because Zhang's strictness makes the strait safe, which makes it valuable, which brings trade. Break any link and it collapses. Wu is the wildcard: his possible Syndicate connections are the one variable Zhang can't fully control, and he keeps Wu precisely because a known risk is better than an unknown one.

institutions.name: The Chain Harbor
institutions.description: Twin stone towers flanking the strait. Chains ready to close in sixty seconds. Li Jun's domain.
institutions.function: Military harbor with chain deployment. No unauthorized passage in 15 years.
institutions.political_leaning: Absolute military control.

institutions.name: The Tea Terraces
institutions.description: Terraced gardens on the fortress's south wall where volcanic soil produces extraordinary tea.
institutions.function: Tea trade — the fortress's economic lifeline. Liu manages production and export.
institutions.political_leaning: Commerce within military constraints.

institutions.name: The Gate Command
institutions.description: The fortress's highest tower. Maps of the strait, chain deployment controls, and Zhang's desk — military-neat, one personal item: nothing. He has no personal items.
institutions.function: Absolute military governance. Zhang's word is law.
institutions.political_leaning: Silk Circle military enforcement.

institutions.name: The Gate Inn
institutions.description: Stone building inside fortress walls. Jasmine tea by day, something stronger at night. Wu sees everything and says nothing.
institutions.function: Social pressure valve + intelligence nexus. Wu provides both.
institutions.political_leaning: Discreet. Wu's loyalties are ambiguous by design.

institutions.name: The Strip Room
institutions.description: A brightly lit room where every cargo is examined. Sun's tools: acid tests, magnifying lenses, and an encyclopedic memory for every smuggling technique ever attempted.
institutions.function: Weapons inspection. Zero tolerance. Sun finds everything.
institutions.political_leaning: Fortress security.

institutions.name: The Strait Infirmary
institutions.description: Small but well-equipped. Chen Ling's domain. The eastern strait's only reliable medical care.
institutions.function: Medical care + desperate medicine purchasing. Chen Ling will pay premium for any medical supply.
institutions.political_leaning: Humanitarian within military structure.

institutions.name: The Permitted Desk
institutions.description: Ming's desk with Zhang's framed 'NO' hanging behind it. The most restricted brokerage in the East.
institutions.function: Brokering within Zhang's permissions. Tea, porcelain, medicine. No weapons. No exceptions.
institutions.political_leaning: Commerce in a cage.

npcs.name: Commander Zhang Wei
npcs.title: Gate Commander
npcs.description: A man whose authority is measured in chains — the harbor chains that can close the eastern strait in under a minute. Commander Zhang governs Dragon's Gate as both military commander and civil authority. His word is law, his chains are persuasion, and his fifteen-year record of zero unauthorized passages speaks for itself.
npcs.agenda: Control. Zhang controls the strait. Ships pass when he permits. Weapons do not pass — ever. His fortress exists to prevent armed escalation in the East Indies, and he considers every weapon that enters the strait a personal failure.
npcs.greeting_neutral: "State your cargo. All weapons must be declared. Failure to declare is treated as hostile intent. These are the terms of passage."
npcs.greeting_friendly: "Captain — your record is clean. Passage is granted. But I will still inspect the weapons hold. Protocol serves everyone."
npcs.greeting_hostile: "Full inspection. Full chain deployment. Your ship will not leave this harbor until I am satisfied that no weapons pass through my strait."
npcs.rumor: The last captain who tried to run Zhang's chains is still chained to the seabed as a warning. Zhang considers this proportionate. The strait has been quiet ever since.

relationship_notes.dg_harbor_captain_li: His harbor officer. Runs the dock under Zhang's absolute authority.
relationship_notes.dg_tea_merchant_liu: The tea trade funds the fortress. Zhang tolerates commerce because he must.
relationship_notes.dg_weapons_inspector_sun: His most trusted officer. Sun finds the weapons Zhang can't allow.
relationship_notes.dg_healer_chen_ling: The fortress healer. Zhang respects medicine — soldiers need it.
relationship_notes.dg_inn_keeper_wu: Wu's inn is where soldiers decompress. Zhang allows it because the alternative is desertion.
relationship_notes.dg_broker_ming: Ming brokers what Zhang permits. The boundary is absolute.

npcs.name: Harbor Captain Li Jun
npcs.title: Harbor Captain
npcs.description: A military officer who runs the harbor like a military operation — because it is one. Li Jun coordinates inspections, manages the chain deployment mechanism, and ensures that no ship docks, departs, or moves within the strait without Zhang's approval.
npcs.agenda: The chain. Li Jun's job is ensuring the chains work — that they can close the strait in under sixty seconds. Everything else is secondary to this capability.
npcs.greeting_neutral: "Berth assignment pending inspection. Anchor in the holding area. Inspector Sun will board within the hour."
npcs.greeting_friendly: "Captain — clean record, priority passage. Inspector Sun will do an abbreviated check. You'll be through within two hours."
npcs.greeting_hostile: "Holding area. Indefinite. Commander Zhang has flagged your vessel. Cooperation will determine how long this takes."
npcs.rumor: Li Jun can deploy the harbor chains from memory — he's memorized every winch, every link, every anchor point. In a drill last year, he closed the strait in forty-three seconds. Zhang said 'acceptable.' Li Jun is trying for thirty-five.

relationship_notes.dg_tea_merchant_liu: Tea ships get efficient processing. The fortress needs revenue.
relationship_notes.dg_weapons_inspector_sun: Sun inspects; Li Jun manages the dock flow around inspections.
relationship_notes.dg_inn_keeper_wu: Li Jun drinks there. Quietly. Officers' corner.
relationship_notes.dg_broker_ming: Ming's contracts must be approved by Li Jun before loading begins.

npcs.name: Tea Merchant Liu
npcs.title: Tea Factor
npcs.description: A woman who has learned to trade tea within the framework of a military fortress — which means patience, paperwork, and the understanding that Commander Zhang's approval is required for everything, including breathing. Liu manages Dragon's Gate's tea trade, which is the fortress's economic lifeline.
npcs.agenda: Tea. Liu wants to export the finest tea in the East Indies — and Dragon's Gate's volcanic soil produces extraordinary leaves. She's patient because she has to be, and shrewd because patience alone doesn't pay the fortress's bills.
npcs.greeting_neutral: "Tea? Dragon's Gate produces the finest in the East. I have varieties you won't find elsewhere. The inspection will take time — shall I brew a sample while you wait?"
npcs.greeting_friendly: "Captain! I've been aging a special batch — eighteen months in volcanic clay jars. The flavor is... remarkable. Worth waiting for the inspection."
npcs.greeting_hostile: "Standard tea at posted prices. The premium lots require Commander Zhang's approval. Which requires your record to improve."
npcs.rumor: Liu's volcanic-aged tea was served at a Silk Circle diplomatic banquet. The Circle's magistrates called it the finest they'd ever tasted. Liu didn't mention she ages it in old weapons crates — the iron residue gives it a mineral finish Zhang would definitely not approve of.

relationship_notes.dg_commander_zhang: The tea funds the fortress. He tolerates her commerce.
relationship_notes.dg_weapons_inspector_sun: Sun once accidentally detained a tea shipment for three days. Liu hasn't forgiven him.
relationship_notes.dg_healer_chen_ling: They exchange ingredients. Tea and medicine share more than people think.
relationship_notes.dg_inn_keeper_wu: Wu serves Liu's tea. The soldiers drink it. The cycle funds everything.
relationship_notes.dg_broker_ming: Ming brokers Liu's export contracts. A necessary partnership.

npcs.name: Inspector Sun
npcs.title: Weapons Inspector
npcs.description: The man who finds weapons. Inspector Sun has a reputation that extends across the entire East Indies — if you're smuggling weapons through the Gate, Sun will find them. He's found weapons hidden in grain barrels, sewn into sail canvas, disguised as ship's hardware, and once, memorably, dissolved in acid and stored as liquid iron. He found that too.
npcs.agenda: Zero tolerance. Sun doesn't inspect for tariffs or quality. He inspects for weapons. Every blade, every barrel, every ingot of iron that could be reforged. His fifteen-year record of zero unauthorized passages is Commander Zhang's greatest pride and Sun's only motivation.
npcs.greeting_neutral: "Weapons declaration. Full manifest. I will inspect the hold personally. Cooperation determines speed."
npcs.greeting_friendly: "Captain — your record is clean. Abbreviated inspection. But I will still check the forward hold. Protocol respects no friendship."
npcs.greeting_hostile: "Full strip inspection. Every hold, every compartment, every barrel. I've found weapons in places you can't imagine. Don't test me."
npcs.rumor: Sun found weapons dissolved in acid and stored as liquid iron. The smuggler was a chemist. Sun is not a chemist — but he noticed the acid smell was wrong for the declared cargo of vinegar. He tested one drop. The smuggler is in chains. Sun considers this a normal Tuesday.

relationship_notes.dg_commander_zhang: His commander and the man whose record he protects with every inspection.
relationship_notes.dg_harbor_captain_li: They coordinate: Sun inspects, Li Jun manages the queue.
relationship_notes.dg_tea_merchant_liu: He once detained her tea for three days. She hasn't forgiven him. He doesn't care.
relationship_notes.dg_healer_chen_ling: Medicine shipments pass quickly — Sun has no quarrel with healing.
relationship_notes.dg_inn_keeper_wu: Sun doesn't drink. He watches the inn for weapons deals. Wu knows. It keeps both honest.
relationship_notes.dg_broker_ming: Every contract Ming brokers must pass Sun's review. No exceptions.

npcs.name: Healer Chen Ling
npcs.title: Fortress Healer
npcs.description: A woman whose gentle hands have tended fortress soldiers and civilian sailors alike for twenty years. Chen Ling runs Dragon's Gate's infirmary — a small but well-equipped facility that serves as the eastern strait's only reliable medical care.
